traditions.title: Summer, boats and barbecues
traditions.text: In Australia the New Year comes at the height of summer: on the beach, in a park, on a boat or by the grill at home. At midnight: fireworks and a glass of champagne.

traditions.title: Two shows over the Torrens
traditions.text: Elder Park has two shows: a family one at 9 pm and the main one at midnight. In 2025 entry was free and the park held up to 25,000 people.

traditions.title: Midnight at Glenelg beach
traditions.text: At Glenelg and Brighton on the gulf shore, fireworks set to music go up at 9:30 pm; at midnight, at Glenelg only. Entry is free, and the jetties close for the night.

AZ.text:
In Azerbaijan the last evening of the year is a double celebration: 31 December is also World Azerbaijanis Solidarity Day, so it is a day off, and 1 and 2 January are the New Year holiday. Many customs date from Soviet times: families decorate a New Year tree, gather around a festive table, and children get presents from Shakhta Baba (Grandfather Frost) and Gar Gyz (the Snow Girl). Before midnight the President addresses the nation, and at midnight the anthem plays on every TV channel.

In Baku the place to be is the Seaside Boulevard on the Caspian. Last December it hosted a fair with hot drinks and the city’s first open-air ice rink. At midnight the city’s fireworks burst over the boulevard, while on the hill above the bay the Flame Towers glow, their LED facades showing fire and the colours of the flag.

traditions.title: Tree and Shakhta Baba
traditions.text: Decorate the tree ahead of time and sit down to a festive dinner with family on 31 December. Shakhta Baba and Gar Gyz bring the children their presents.

traditions.title: Address and anthem at midnight
traditions.text: The last minutes of the year are spent by the TV: after the President’s greeting, Azerbaijan’s anthem plays on every channel.

traditions.title: Fireworks on Baku’s boulevard
traditions.text: Crowds gather on the Seaside Boulevard by the Caspian: last December it had a fair and an ice rink, and at midnight fireworks burst over the bay.

meta.title: New Year 2027: Baku, Azerbaijan | Time2Fest
meta.description: Baku, Azerbaijan, rings in 2027 with fireworks over the Seaside Boulevard by the Caspian, Shakhta Baba and the glowing Flame Towers. Midnight: 20:00 UTC.

BR@utc-0500.text:
Brazil welcomes the New Year — Réveillon — in white. The custom began with Candomblé followers who, in the 1970s, came to Copacabana beach in white with gifts for Iemanjá, the water goddess; since then white clothes and flowers set out to sea have spread across the country. At midnight people on the coast jump seven waves, making a wish on each.

Rio Branco, capital of the state of Acre, greets the year last in Brazil — two hours after Rio. In 2026 the city hall threw a free party on Praça da Revolução in the centre: local bands, a countdown and fireworks right at midnight. The fireworks here are quiet: state law bans bangers to protect children, older people and animals.

traditions.title: In white, like all of Brazil
traditions.text: At New Year most people dress in white. The custom comes from Afro-Brazilian religions and long ago spread across the whole country.

traditions.title: Fireworks without bangs
traditions.text: Since 2022 Acre has banned fireworks that go bang — only ones that simply light up are allowed. Midnight is bright but quiet for animals and autistic people.

traditions.title: Praça da Revolução
traditions.text: In 2026 the city hall gathered families for a free party in the city centre: bands from six in the evening, a countdown and fireworks at midnight sharp.

LT.text:
Lithuania greets the New Year with old customs. It once belonged to the winter feasts running from Christmas Eve to Three Kings: masked mummers staged a duel between the old year and the new, and in Samogitia young people burned a sheaf of straw as the old year. At midnight people told fortunes, pouring melted wax into water and reading the shapes: a wheel means a journey, a cradle a child. Small children were woken at twelve sharp so they would not sleep through their luck.

In Vilnius people like to meet midnight outdoors, on Cathedral Square, by the city Christmas tree, the cathedral and its bell tower, with Gediminas Tower on the hill above. The city has skipped fireworks for several years: last year colourful videos were projected onto the bell tower from 10 p.m., and at midnight a light show swept the square.

traditions.title: Reading the wax
traditions.text: At midnight pour a little melted wax into cold water and study the shape: a wheel means a journey, a cradle a new arrival in the family.

traditions.title: Don’t sleep through your luck
traditions.text: By old custom nobody sleeps on New Year’s night, and small children are woken at twelve sharp so the year’s luck won’t pass them by.

traditions.title: Lights on Cathedral Square
traditions.text: In Vilnius people meet midnight by the Christmas tree: instead of fireworks there are colourful projections on the bell tower and a light show. Pyrotechnics near churches are banned by law.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Lithuania: Vilnius | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Vilnius, 22:00 UTC, Lithuania meets 2027 with a light show on Cathedral Square instead of fireworks, while at home melted wax tells fortunes.

BR@utc-0200.text:

At midnight people on the coast jump seven waves, making a wish on each.

Fernando de Noronha, an Atlantic archipelago, is the only inhabited place in Brazil on UTC−2, so midnight arrives here an hour before Rio. The main party is the Réveillon da Ilha on Praia do Porto: 2026 began with a concert by the singer Silva, and the celebrations ran over three days. Above it all rises Morro do Pico, a 323 m rock and the archipelago's highest point.

traditions.title: White, like all Brazil
traditions.text: Wear white to see the year in, as almost all of Brazil does. The custom comes from Candomblé and Umbanda.

traditions.title: Seven waves, seven wishes
traditions.text: At midnight, people step into the surf and jump seven waves, making a wish on each: seven is a sacred number in Umbanda.

traditions.title: Réveillon da Ilha
traditions.text: The island's party on Praia do Porto: concerts by Brazilian and local musicians on 31 December, 1 and 3 January.

AU@utc+0800.text:
In Australia New Year's Eve is a summer night, so it is spent outdoors: on a beach or in a park, on a boat, at a concert or at home by the barbecue with friends. Cities greet midnight with fireworks, and glasses are filled with champagne or wine. 31 December itself is an ordinary working day, but 1 January is a holiday across the country.

Perth, the capital of Western Australia, welcomes the year three hours after Sydney. Two fireworks shows go up over Elizabeth Quay on the Swan River, at 8.30 pm and at midnight; in 2025, according to the City of Perth, about 130,000 people came into the centre. Nearby on Barrack Square stands the Swan Bells tower; 12 of its bells came from St Martin-in-the-Fields in London.

traditions.title: Two shows over Elizabeth Quay
traditions.text: Over the Elizabeth Quay inlet on the Swan River there are two shows: at 8.30 pm for families with children and the main one at midnight. Northbridge fires its own at midnight too.

traditions.title: Midnight three hours later
traditions.text: Western Australia does not use daylight saving: 54.6% voted no in the 2009 referendum. When Sydney is already celebrating it is only 9 pm in Perth, and midnight comes at 16:00 UTC.

traditions.title: The view from Langley Park
traditions.text: The fireworks are easy to see from Langley Park and Birdiya Drive by the Convention Centre. Getting home is free: in 2025 buses and trains ran all night, with free travel from midnight to 6 am.

AU@utc+0845.text:
In Australia 31 December is midsummer, so New Year's night is spent mostly outdoors: on beaches, in parks, on boats or at home around the barbecue. At midnight fireworks burst over the cities and people raise a glass of champagne or wine. The day itself is a working day, but on 1 January the whole country has the day off.

Eucla is a settlement on the Nullarbor Plain, 11 km from the South Australian border. It grew up in 1877 around a telegraph station whose ruins still stand in the dunes. Here and at nearby roadhouses along the Eyre Highway, clocks unofficially run 45 minutes ahead of Perth.

traditions.title: Three clocks on the wall
traditions.text: At the border checkpoint and above the Eucla Motel entrance hang three clocks: Adelaide, Perth and Eucla time. Phones here show Perth time, so locals count down to Eucla's midnight by the clock on the wall or set their phones by hand.

traditions.title: The year's last sunset
traditions.text: The Eucla Motel sits on the escarpment above the Great Australian Bight, and from the pub deck you can watch the sun set into the ocean. Its restaurant is open every night.

traditions.title: New Year's Day at Bunda Cliffs
traditions.text: 1 January is a public holiday, a good day to drive east along the Eyre Highway to the lookouts. The limestone Bunda Cliffs, 60–120 metres high, run for 210 km along the Bight.

AU@utc+0930.text:
In Australia, New Year is a summer night spent outdoors. People head to concerts and parties, to beaches and city parks, take a boat out on the water or invite friends round for a backyard barbecue. At midnight fireworks burst over the cities and glasses are filled with champagne or wine. 1 January is a public holiday in every state and territory, while 31 December is an ordinary working day.

Darwin, the capital of the Northern Territory, celebrates at the Darwin Waterfront. It is the biggest family party of the tropical Top End: free entry, a concert, picnics and two fireworks displays, at 9 pm and at midnight. Further south, in the Central Australian desert of the same territory, rises Uluru, a 348-metre rock sacred to the Anangu people.

traditions.title: A toast under summer skies
traditions.text: New Year here is spent outdoors: on the beach, in a park, on a boat or round the grill with friends. At midnight come the fireworks and a glass of champagne or wine.

traditions.title: Two shows at the Waterfront
traditions.text: Darwin’s waterfront has fireworks twice: at 9 pm for families with children and the main show at midnight. Entry is free and picnics are welcome, but alcohol and smoking are not.

traditions.title: Midnight 90 minutes later
traditions.text: The Northern Territory does not use daylight saving time. So when Sydney is already celebrating, Darwin still has an hour and a half to go: midnight here falls at 14:30 UTC.

US@utc-1000.text:
Hawaii runs on UTC−10 and never changes its clocks, so the New Year arrives here five hours after New York. At midnight the islands crackle with firecrackers and fireworks, meant to chase away evil spirits. Japanese plantation workers brought mochi in the mid-1800s: families pound rice together in a wooden mortar and eat ozoni, a soup with mochi and vegetables, for good luck. The greeting is “Hauʻoli Makahiki Hou”, Hawaiian for “Happy New Year”.

In Honolulu the midnight fireworks burst over Waikiki Beach, where people set up chairs and blankets on the sand or watch from hotel balconies. On 1 January a First Day Hike at the Kaʻiwi shoreline opens with the call of a conch shell and a sunrise prayer.

traditions.title: Firecrackers need a permit
traditions.text: On Oʻahu firecrackers are allowed only from 9 p.m. to 1 a.m. and only with a $25 permit, good for up to 5,000 of them. Aerials, sparklers and fountains are banned.

traditions.title: Mochi and ozoni soup
traditions.text: Mochi is pounded as a family: it is hard work that takes many hands. For the holiday people eat ozoni, a clear broth with mochi, vegetables and fish cake, for luck in the new year.

traditions.title: A blanket on Waikiki Beach
traditions.text: Honolulu’s midnight fireworks are best seen right from Waikiki Beach, where people come with chairs and blankets. The biggest crowds gather near the Hilton Hawaiian Village.

US@utc-0600.text:
In the Central zone of the United States, from Chicago to New Orleans, midnight arrives an hour after New York. People count down with TV specials and sing Auld Lang Syne at midnight. In Nashville a red music note descends a 138-foot tower at a free concert that drew 205,000 people in 2025. In New Orleans a fleur-de-lis drops from a French Quarter rooftop as fireworks burst over the Mississippi. On 1 January the South eats black-eyed peas and collard greens for luck.

For 2026, New Year’s Rockin’ Eve ran its first Central Time countdown from Chicago, with fireworks launched from the river bridges. At midnight Navy Pier adds a free 10-minute show over Lake Michigan.

traditions.title: A note and a fleur-de-lis
traditions.text: Instead of a ball, Central cities drop their own symbols: Nashville a red music note with 28,000 LEDs, New Orleans a fleur-de-lis from a French Quarter rooftop. Both parties are free.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the water
traditions.text: In Chicago, midnight fireworks rise over Lake Michigan by Navy Pier, and for 2026 they also flew from the river bridges. In New Orleans you can watch them from both banks of the Mississippi.

traditions.title: Peas and greens for luck
traditions.text: 1 January is a federal holiday. In the South it means black-eyed peas, red beans and rice and collard greens, and the New Orleans fireworks even play college fight songs for Sugar Bowl fans.

US@utc-0700.text:
In the Mountain time zone of the United States, from Montana to Arizona, midnight comes two hours after New York. Here too people sing Auld Lang Syne at midnight, and Colorado’s ski resorts mark the night their own way: in Breckenridge instructors ski down the slope with red flares, and in Steamboat Springs fireworks follow a torchlight parade. In Boise a crane lowers a giant potato more than five metres long into the crowd moments before midnight. 1 January is a federal holiday, and many people set out on a First Day Hike in a state park.

In Denver fireworks rise over downtown twice, at 9 p.m. and at midnight, and the best view is from 16th Street. That night RTD buses and trains are free.

traditions.title: Torches on the slopes
traditions.text: At Colorado resorts on New Year’s Eve, instructors ski down with torches: in Breckenridge a red snake of flares crosses the mountain at 6 p.m. Fireworks over the valley follow the parade.

traditions.title: Two shows over Denver
traditions.text: The free show launches from downtown rooftops at 9 p.m. and again at midnight; it’s easy to see from 16th Street. From 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. RTD buses and trains are free.

traditions.title: A First Day Hike
traditions.text: 1 January is a day off, and state parks across the country hold First Day Hikes. In the Mountain zone that means a walk among snowy peaks and red rock.

US@utc-0900.text:
Alaska greets the New Year four hours after New York, and in long winter darkness: on 31 December the sun sets in Anchorage at 3:51 p.m. Because of the cold, fireworks here often go up well before midnight, and at Alyeska ski resort skiers come down the slope carrying torches before fireworks light up the mountain at 9 p.m. On clear winter nights the northern lights often dance over Fairbanks. At midnight, as everywhere in the US, people sing Auld Lang Syne, and 1 January is a federal holiday.

In Anchorage a free downtown party gathers people at 3rd Avenue and E Street, with a sledding hill, food trucks, hot toddies and fire dancers. Fireworks rise over Cook Inlet at 8 p.m., exactly when midnight strikes in New York. Personal fireworks are banned in the city, so this is the only show.

traditions.title: Torches at Alyeska
traditions.text: At Alyeska Resort near Anchorage, skiers come down the slope with torches on New Year’s Eve. Right after, at 9 p.m., fireworks burst over the mountain.

traditions.title: Fireworks at 8 p.m.
traditions.text: Anchorage’s only official fireworks go up at 8 p.m., so families with children can come despite the cold. From 7 to 9 p.m. downtown has a sledding hill and food trucks; in 2025 organisers expected about 10,000 people.

traditions.title: A First Day Hike
traditions.text: 1 January is a day off, and state parks across the country hold First Day Hikes. In Alaska people set out near noon: in late December Anchorage gets less than six hours of daylight.

CL@utc-0500.text:
Chile sees in the New Year at the height of summer, so many people celebrate on the beach. At the family dinner there are lentils for luck, at midnight twelve grapes, yellow underwear is a must, and anyone dreaming of travel walks around the block with a suitcase. Selling fireworks to individuals has been banned since 2000, so the fireworks here are official only.

Rapa Nui, or Easter Island, lies 3,512 km from the mainland, and midnight arrives two hours after Santiago, the last in Chile. In Hanga Roa, restaurants host New Year's Eve dinners with live music and Rapa Nui songs and dances, and after dinner people head to the fireworks at Hanga Vare Vare.

traditions.title: Grapes and yellow underwear
traditions.text: At midnight eat twelve grapes, one with a wish for each month. Yellow underwear brings joy and money.

traditions.title: Dinner with Rapa Nui songs
traditions.text: In Hanga Roa, New Year's Eve dinners come with live music and Rapa Nui songs and dances, then people walk to the fireworks at Hanga Vare Vare.

traditions.title: Sunset and sunrise by the moai
traditions.text: The year's last sunset is watched by the moai at Tahai, where no guide is needed. On 1 January, Tongariki opens at sunrise, but only with a park ticket and a local guide.

ID@utc+0800.text:
Central Indonesia — Bali, Sulawesi, southern and eastern Kalimantan and the Lesser Sunda Islands — sees in the New Year an hour before Jakarta. As everywhere in the country, people blow terompet horns, grill chicken or corn and sit down to a family meal. On Bali they head for the sea: on the eve of 2026 about 18,500 people gathered in Canggu and 12,000 in Kuta. That year fireworks were called off almost everywhere out of sympathy for flood victims in Sumatra, and many prayed together at midnight. 1 January is a holiday across the country.

In Makassar everyone makes for the Losari waterfront. From ten in the evening the crowd grows until it stretches all the way to old Fort Rotterdam, and the first fireworks go up before midnight.

traditions.title: A night by the sea in Bali
traditions.text: On Bali the New Year is met on the beaches of Canggu and Kuta and in the GWK cultural park. Whether there are fireworks is decided each time: for 2026 they were replaced by a shared prayer at midnight.

traditions.title: An evening of art in Denpasar
traditions.text: Instead of fireworks, Denpasar marked the arrival of 2026 with a free evening of Balinese art on Puputan Badung square. The city's own art studios performed.

traditions.title: Fireworks from a phinisi deck
traditions.text: In Makassar, fireworks go up at midnight on the Losari waterfront and at Center Point of Indonesia. Some people launch them straight from the decks of phinisi sailing ships moored by the shore.

ID@utc+0900.text:
Indonesia's east — the Maluku Islands and Papua — welcomes the New Year before the rest of the country. For Christians, the evening of 31 December begins in church: in Ambon the night is called 'konci taong', locking up the year, and after the service people pour into the streets. At midnight the ships anchored in Ambon Bay sound their horns, church bells and mosque drums answer, and fireworks fill the sky over the city and the hills. 1 January is a holiday across Indonesia.

In Jayapura people gather every year by the Youtefa Bridge: families arrive from nine in the evening and set off their own fireworks at midnight. Cafes along the Hamadi–Holtekamp road stay open late, and in the yards neighbours grill fish together over the fire.

traditions.title: A service to close the year
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December Christians in Ambon and Jayapura go to church for a service that sees out the year. Afterwards the celebration moves to the streets.

traditions.title: Ship horns at midnight
traditions.text: In Ambon, at exactly 00:00, the ships anchored in the bay sound their horns. Church bells and the beduk drums of the mosques answer them.

traditions.title: Grilled fish with the neighbours
traditions.text: In Jayapura, before midnight, neighbours grill fish together outdoors and everyone brings something to the shared table. That way children see in the year close to their family.

MX@utc-0500.text:
Mexico sees out the year over a late family dinner, and at midnight eats a grape with each of the twelve chimes, making a wish every time, a custom that came from Spain. Before midnight the house is swept out towards the street to drive away the bad, a plate of lentils and rice goes on the table for abundance, and the colour of new underwear calls in love, money or health. After the twelfth chime comes a shout of «¡Feliz Año Nuevo!» and firecrackers and sparklers light up.

Quintana Roo has had its own time zone since 2015, so Cancún is the first place in the country to greet the year, an hour ahead of central Mexico. Last year the city party on the Malecón Tajamar waterfront ran from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.: five bands and, instead of pyrotechnics, a drone show. That night the fireworks went up over nearby Isla Mujeres.

traditions.title: Sweep out the old year
traditions.text: Before midnight, sweep from the back room to the door and out into the street, the way Mexicans chase off the bad of the old year.

traditions.title: Lentils for plenty
traditions.text: Put a plate of lentils and rice on the festive table, or tuck a few lentils into your wallet, for a full and generous year.

traditions.title: A night on Malecón Tajamar
traditions.text: In Cancún, the party is on the Malecón Tajamar waterfront: last year bands played there until 5 a.m. and a drone show lit up midnight.

CA@utc-0330.text:
Canada sees in the New Year differently in each province, but some customs are known nationwide. In Quebec, on the evening of 31 December, people watch Bye Bye, Radio-Canada's comedy review of the year, which since 1968 has ended with the countdown to midnight. And on 1 January the Governor General and the provincial lieutenant governors hold levees, New Year receptions open to anyone, children included.

Newfoundland keeps its own time: it is the only zone in the Americas with a half-hour offset, so midnight arrives half an hour earlier than in the rest of Atlantic Canada. Last year St. John's celebrated outdoors on George Street, with music and midnight pyrotechnics. And over the Christmas days, disguised mummers still go from house to house.

traditions.title: The lieutenant governor's levee
traditions.text: On 1 January the provincial lieutenant governor, like the Governor General, receives New Year guests: the doors are open to everyone, children included.

traditions.title: Mummers at the door
traditions.text: During the Christmas days disguised visitors knock on doors: hosts let them in, offer a drink and try to guess who is behind the mask.

traditions.title: Countdown on George Street
traditions.text: Last year the outdoor party in downtown St. John's was free for all ages: live music, DJs and pyrotechnics at midnight.

CA@utc-0400.text:
Canada sees in the New Year a little differently in each province, though some customs unite the whole country. In Quebec people watch Bye Bye on 31 December, Radio-Canada’s comedy review of the year, aired since 1968 and ending with the countdown to midnight. On 1 January the provincial lieutenant governors and military units hold levees, New Year receptions open to everyone; the first one in Canada took place back in 1646.

Last year Halifax celebrated outdoors in Grand Parade: DJs and musicians played from 11 pm, fireworks went up at midnight and city transit ran free. In the morning Government House, the oldest vice-regal residence in North America, welcomes visitors, and in Dartmouth hundreds of people plunge into a pool cut in the ice of Lake Banook.

traditions.title: Count down in Grand Parade
traditions.text: Halifax’s free city party downtown starts at 11 pm and ends with fireworks at midnight; free transit will take you home.

traditions.title: Levee at Government House
traditions.text: On 1 January the lieutenant governor opens the doors to everyone, no invitation needed; about 700 guests come each year. New Brunswick holds its own levee too.

traditions.title: The plunge at Banook
traditions.text: On 1 January in Dartmouth a big pool is cut in the ice, and hundreds of brave souls jump in while friends cheer from the shore.

MX@utc-0700.text:
Mexico greets the New Year with twelve grapes: at midnight people eat one with each chime of the clock and make a wish every time, a custom that came from Spain. Earlier in the evening the house is swept out all the way to the street to clear away the bad of the old year, and the colour of new underwear hints at the wish: red for love, yellow for money, green for health. After the twelfth chime comes “¡Feliz Año Nuevo!”, fireworks and firecrackers go up, and someone is already running round the block with a suitcase to bring a year of travel.

The Pacific zone — Sinaloa, Sonora, Nayarit and Baja California Sur — sees in the year an hour after Mexico City. In Mazatlán last year the city threw the party right on the Malecón, a seafront promenade about 8.5 km long: from 9 p.m. there was live music by the giant letters spelling the city’s name, a drone show and fireworks. Local media reported more than 40,000 people.

traditions.title: Twelve wishes
traditions.text: Get twelve grapes ready: at midnight eat one on each stroke of the clock and make a wish every time.

traditions.title: Sweep out the old year
traditions.text: Before midnight sweep the house from the rooms to the door and out into the street to chase away whatever bad the old year left behind.

traditions.title: Midnight on the Malecón
traditions.text: In Mazatlán the party is on the seafront by the city’s giant letters: last year there was live music from 9 p.m., a drone show and fireworks, all free.

MX@utc-0800.text:
Mexico sees out the year over a late family dinner: turkey or pork loin, or, depending on the region, tamales, pozole or bacalao. At midnight people eat a grape on each of the twelve chimes and make a wish every time, while the colour of new underwear calls in what you want: red for love, yellow for money, green for health. Before midnight the house is swept out right to the door so nothing bad follows into the new year.

Baja California is the only state in the UTC−8 zone, so Tijuana is the last place in Mexico to greet the year, two hours after Mexico City. Selling and setting off fireworks are both banned here, and the city suggests light wands and string lights instead. The real party is at home around the table: last year, according to the newspaper El Imparcial, families spent up to 5,000 pesos on the dinner.

traditions.title: A suitcase for the road
traditions.text: As soon as midnight strikes, some people take a suitcase and walk round the block: they say the further you go, the further you will travel this year.

traditions.title: Light instead of firecrackers
traditions.text: In Tijuana fireworks may be neither sold nor set off. Grab a light wand or LED string lights, and keep your pets indoors somewhere quiet.

traditions.title: Rosca by the Cecut dome
traditions.text: The celebrations go on past New Year’s Eve: last year, on 10 January, a giant Three Kings rosca was shared for free around the IMAX dome of the Tijuana Cultural Centre.

US@utc-0800.text:
The Pacific zone of the United States, from Seattle and San Francisco to Los Angeles and Las Vegas, welcomes the New Year three hours after New York. Since 2000 Las Vegas has thrown America’s Party on the Strip: for 2025 the Sphere, the world’s largest LED screen, led the countdown for the first time, followed by eight minutes of fireworks from the rooftops of nine resorts. In San Francisco free midnight fireworks light up the Bay by the Ferry Building on the Embarcadero, and in Seattle a drone show gives way to fireworks over the Space Needle.

In Los Angeles, Grand Park hosts the free NYELA party, and at midnight the countdown glows on City Hall. On the morning of 1 January neighbouring Pasadena starts the 138th Rose Parade.

traditions.title: Walk the Strip at midnight
traditions.text: On New Year’s Eve the Las Vegas Strip closes to cars and the boulevard fills with people on foot. At midnight fireworks fly from resort rooftops for eight minutes; last year large bags were not allowed.

traditions.title: Fireworks over bay and tower
traditions.text: In San Francisco the free fireworks look best from the Embarcadero just south of the Ferry Building. In Seattle people watch from Seattle Center, on the lawn by the International Fountain.

traditions.title: A morning at the Rose Parade
traditions.text: 1 January is a federal holiday. At 8 a.m. the Rose Parade sets off in Pasadena: flower-covered floats roll 9 km, and some people hold their spot on the sidewalk from the night of 31 December.

ES@utc+0000.text:
In Spain the New Year arrives with grapes: at midnight people eat twelve of them to the twelve chimes of the clock, one per chime, for luck and prosperity. Then comes a glass of cava, sometimes with a gold ring at the bottom, drunk in one go. But since 1940 the Canary Islands have lived an hour behind the mainland, and Spaniards are used to hearing on radio and TV: «una hora menos en Canarias» — one hour less in the Canaries.

So on the islands the grapes are eaten when Madrid is already celebrating. Since the night 1984 began, state television has shown the Canarian midnight an hour after Puerta del Sol, each time from a different island; 2026 was welcomed in Plaza de la Candelaria in Santa Cruz de Tenerife. In Las Palmas de Gran Canaria fireworks rise over Las Canteras beach at midnight, and on the afternoon of 31 December the San Silvestre race runs through the city.

traditions.title: Grapes an hour later
traditions.text: One grape for each of the twelve chimes, for a lucky year. Midnight in the Canaries comes an hour after Madrid, so television shows the islands' chimes separately.

traditions.title: A gold ring in the glass
traditions.text: After the grapes, raise a glass of cava: a gold ring or coin goes in for prosperity, a strawberry for love. Then drink it in one go.

traditions.title: Fireworks over Las Canteras
traditions.text: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria welcomed 2026 with fireworks launched from Los Muellitos over Las Canteras beach. That night's free concerts played behind Parque de Santa Catalina.

WS.text:
Samoa is one of the first countries in the world to see the new year. That began at the end of 2011, when the country moved to the other side of the date line and simply skipped 30 December, so midnight here falls at 11:00 UTC. For many families the old year ends in church: evening services start at nine or eleven, and the last minutes of the year are spent in prayer. 1 and 2 January are public holidays.

Apia is the capital, on the north coast of Upolu island. People claim their spots early on the seawall by the Government Building, count down the last twenty seconds, and at midnight a ten-minute fireworks show rises from Palisi hill above the centre. Bells ring and sirens sound across town, and the Prime Minister addresses the nation with a New Year message.

traditions.title: A service until midnight
traditions.text: Many families see the year out in church: the service begins in the evening, and the congregation prays together through the last minutes before midnight to give thanks for the year.

traditions.title: Fireworks from Palisi
traditions.text: In Apia people take their places on the seawall hours ahead to watch the fireworks from the hill above the centre. Away from downtown, children line the streets with their own small crackers.

traditions.title: A week of prayer and fasting
traditions.text: On the first Sunday of January the government opens a national week of prayer and fasting. The custom dates from 1990, after Cyclone Ofa struck: people ask for protection for Samoa through the year.

meta.title: New Year in Samoa: Apia | Time2Fest
meta.description: Samoa greets 2027 among the very first: midnight in Apia is at 11:00 UTC. Families pray in church, then watch fireworks over Palisi hill from the seawall.

CA@utc-0700.text:
Each Canadian province greets the New Year a little differently, but a few customs bring the country together. On 31 December Quebec settles in front of the TV for Bye Bye, Radio-Canada's comedy review of the year, aired since 1968 and ending with the countdown to midnight. On 1 January the Governor General and the provincial lieutenant governors hold levees, New Year receptions open to anyone.

Since 2026 British Columbia has kept permanent Pacific time, UTC−7. Vancouver has had no city fireworks since 2018, so people count down on their own outside Canada Place and at the Gastown Steam Clock, or head up Grouse Mountain. On 1 January thousands plunge into English Bay.

traditions.title: The governor's levee
traditions.text: On 1 January anyone can walk into a New Year's levee, children too: guests shake the host's hand and wish them a good year.

traditions.title: Midnight on a mountain
traditions.text: Last year on Grouse Mountain above Vancouver people skated to a DJ, and at midnight fireworks set to music lit up the summit.

traditions.title: The Polar Bear Swim
traditions.text: Every 1 January since 1920 Vancouver has plunged into chilly English Bay; it is free, and more than 11,000 swimmers registered last year.

CA@utc-0600.text:
Canada sees in the New Year differently in each province, but a few customs are known across the country. In Quebec people watch Bye Bye on 31 December, the comedy review of the year that Radio-Canada has aired since 1968; last year more than four million viewers tuned in. On 1 January the provincial lieutenant governors hold levees, New Year receptions open to anyone.

In Edmonton, Alberta's capital, last year's party was on Churchill Square: music, a rink with free skate rentals and two fireworks shows, at 8 pm for little ones and at midnight. Next to the arena in the Ice District, a concert and a DJ set followed the Oilers game. In Calgary that night people danced on the ice of the Prince's Island lagoon until the midnight fireworks lit up the Bow.

traditions.title: Dancing at a Malanka
traditions.text: In January the Ukrainian communities of Edmonton and Winnipeg hold Malankas, Old New Year galas with dinner, live music and dancing late into the night.

traditions.title: Skating, then fireworks
traditions.text: In Edmonton and Calgary the city party is free: people skate to music, and families with kids come by 8 pm, when Edmonton sets off an early fireworks show.

traditions.title: The New Year's levee
traditions.text: On 1 January Alberta's lieutenant governor opens Government House in Edmonton to all: refreshments, a tour and a postcard for Canadian troops abroad.

FJ.text:
Fiji is among the first places in the world to see the new year: midnight here falls at 12:00 UTC. On the islands the holiday is called Na Vakatawase, the ‘division’ between the old year and the new. Many people see the year out in church, and once the service ends, veisui begins: friends, family and even passers-by are splashed with water to wash away the bad of the past year, then wrapped in dry cloth. In villages the mood often lasts all of January.

Suva is the capital, on a hilly peninsula on the southeast coast of Viti Levu. On the evening of 31 December, hundreds of families and young people from across the island head to Albert Park in the city centre: music, a countdown of the final seconds, and fireworks bursting over the park at midnight.

traditions.title: A splash for a fresh start
traditions.text: After midnight, family and friends get splashed with water to wash off the bad of the old year. Whoever is soaked is wrapped in dry cloth or dressed in dry clothes straight away.

traditions.title: Thanks in church
traditions.text: For many Fijians the year ends at a church service, giving thanks at midnight for everything it brought. Plenty travel back to their home village to welcome the New Year with family.

traditions.title: New Year's Day by the water
traditions.text: 1 January is a public holiday, and families across the country head to parks, beaches and swimming spots to start the year together, with a picnic and a swim.

meta.title: New Year in Fiji: Suva | Time2Fest
meta.description: Fiji greets 2027 among the first: midnight in Suva is at 12:00 UTC. After church, families splash each other with water as fireworks rise over Albert Park.

KI.text:
Kiribati is one of the first countries to welcome the New Year, though not all at once: the country spans three time zones. The Line Islands, with Kiritimati, open the year first at UTC+14, then come the Phoenix Islands, and two hours after Kiritimati the Gilbert Islands. Life here rests on family, church and the sea, so from Christmas to New Year there are choirs, dancing, canoe races and other contests.

Tarawa in the Gilbert Islands is the capital, home to more than half the country: a string of islets between the lagoon and the ocean, joined by causeways. It is also home to parliament, called the Maneaba ni Maungatabu after the maneaba, the traditional meeting house. Tarawa sees in the New Year at church services, then celebrates quietly with family or at small parties on the beach.

traditions.title: A church service at midnight
traditions.text: In Tarawa the New Year begins in church, followed by quiet celebrations with family. Church is one of the three pillars of life here, alongside family and the sea.

traditions.title: The frigatebird dance
traditions.text: The holidays mean choirs and dancing. Dancers spread their arms and snap their heads like the frigatebird on the flag, while men beat the rhythm on a wooden box.

traditions.title: Canoes and a beach night
traditions.text: From Christmas to New Year the atoll holds canoe races and other contests, and on 31 December people gather for small parties on the beaches between lagoon and ocean.

meta.title: New Year in Tarawa, Kiribati | Time2Fest
meta.description: Tarawa, the capital of Kiribati, greets 2027 at midnight UTC+12, which is 12:00 UTC: church services, choirs, frigatebird dances, canoe races and beach nights.

TK.text:
Tokelau is three low atolls in the Pacific Ocean, home to about 1,500 people at the 2016 census, and one of the first places the new year reaches. That began at the end of 2011: following Samoa, the islands moved to the other side of the date line and simply skipped 30 December. Christmas and New Year are public holidays and the time when families come home — though there is no airport, so the trip from Apia takes over a day by ship.

Fakaofo was once the heart of the celebration: in May the people of all the islands gathered here for the old new year, with a feast and dancing through the night. The atoll's main village is Fale, and in 2012 solar plants went live on all three atolls, making Tokelau the world's first territory powered entirely by the sun.

traditions.title: Home for the holidays
traditions.text: Before Christmas and New Year, Tokelauans sail home from Apia on the MV Mataliki to spend the holidays with family. A barge carries them across the reef to shore.

traditions.title: A service for the new year
traditions.text: The church is at the centre of atoll life: half the people are Congregationalists and over a third are Catholics. In 2021 Tokelau's office in Apia began the year with a service full of Tokelauan customs.

traditions.title: Fatele to the pokihi
traditions.text: The fatele is Tokelau's best-known dance: villages perform it at their gatherings to the pokihi box drum, and the singing grows higher and faster towards the end.

meta.title: New Year in Tokelau: Fakaofo | Time2Fest
meta.description: Tokelau is among the first to see 2027: midnight on Fakaofo atoll falls at 11:00 UTC. Families sail home for the holidays to islands powered by the sun.

TO.text:
Tonga is one of the first countries the new year reaches: the kingdom keeps UTC+13 all year, so midnight here falls at 11:00 UTC. The celebration is quiet and rooted in church: most people see it in at late-night thanksgiving services, and families gather at home and in their villages on Tongatapu, Vava'u, Ha'apai and 'Eua. At midnight church bells ring and crackers pop for a few minutes, and the following week the Free Wesleyan Church prays every morning and evening.

Tongatapu is the main island, flat and made of limestone, home to over 70% of Tongans. In the capital, Nuku'alofa, the King welcomes the year at a service in Saione church, and on 1 January he usually receives guests at the wooden Royal Palace of 1867. In the east of the island stands Ha'amonga 'a Maui, a 13th-century stone gateway.

traditions.title: A midnight service
traditions.text: In Tonga the new year is welcomed in church, at late-night services of thanks for the year gone by. At midnight the bells ring and a brass band plays a hymn.

traditions.title: At home with family
traditions.text: After the service, families gather at home and in their villages on Tongatapu, Vava'u, Ha'apai and 'Eua. It is a quiet night, without big public parties.

traditions.title: A week of prayer
traditions.text: The Free Wesleyan Church gives the first week of the new year to prayer, with services every morning and evening to give thanks and ask blessings for the year ahead.

meta.title: New Year in Tonga: Tongatapu | Time2Fest
meta.description: Tonga greets 2027 among the first: midnight on Tongatapu falls at 11:00 UTC. Late-night church services, bells and a brass-band hymn, then a week of prayer.

FM.text:
Pohnpei, the island that gives its name to a state of the Federated States of Micronesia, keeps UTC+11, so midnight arrives at 13:00 UTC, an hour earlier than on Chuuk and Yap. New Year’s Eve is the biggest holiday of the year here: families cook all day and gather in a big circle. There is usually no countdown to the second; people check a watch, and only then does the night begin.

The moment the new year arrives, children run from house to house beating drums made of tins and asking for candy, while people leaving church shake hands in the street. Until dawn Kolonia rings with car horns and music, and on Sokehs Island there is marching, cross-dressing and water-throwing too. In the east of Pohnpei stand the basalt walls of Nan Madol, a UNESCO site.

traditions.title: Drums made of tins
traditions.text: After midnight children go from house to house in groups, beating home-made drums made of big tins and shouting for candy to be thrown to them.

traditions.title: A feast for the whole clan
traditions.text: Families cook all day to feed the whole extended family, and after midnight neighbours drop in on each other and trade greetings until morning.

traditions.title: Marching and water fights
traditions.text: On Sokehs Island the New Year is greeted with noisy marching and cross-dressing, and groups by the roadside splash water on passing cars.

meta.title: New Year in Micronesia: Pohnpei | Time2Fest
meta.description: Pohnpei greets 2027 at 13:00 UTC, among the first in Micronesia. Children beat drums made of tins and shout for candy, and families celebrate until dawn.

GU.text:
Guam, a Pacific territory of the United States, keeps UTC+10 with no summer time, so midnight arrives here at 14:00 UTC. Private fireworks are banned on the island by law, which makes the New Year fireworks a shared celebration: the Guam Visitors Bureau stages them every year, and people gather on the shore to greet the year together. The CHamoru, the island's Indigenous people, also keep a count of their own: in the ancient lunar calendar the year begins with the month of Tumaiguini, a time for setting goals.

In Hagåtña, the capital, and in the resort district of Tumon, fireworks rise at midnight over both bays at once. Residents claim a spot at Ypao Beach Park, and before midnight going into 2023 a drone show also flew over the bay.

traditions.title: Fireworks over two bays
traditions.text: On the stroke of midnight fireworks go up over Tumon Bay and Hagåtña Bay at once, lasting around a quarter of an hour.

traditions.title: Midnight at Ypao Beach
traditions.text: Guam residents greet the year at Ypao Beach Park in Tumon; swimming in the bay is discouraged that night, as the fireworks are launched over it.

traditions.title: The CHamoru new year
traditions.text: The ancient CHamoru year begins with the month of Tumaiguini; at its start people walk in pilgrimage to Fouha Rock in Humåtak with offerings for the ancestors.

meta.title: New Year in Guam: Hagåtña | Time2Fest
meta.description: Guam greets 2027 at 14:00 UTC. At midnight fireworks rise over Tumon Bay and Hagåtña Bay at once, as island residents gather at Ypao Beach Park.

MH.text:
The Marshall Islands keep a single time zone, UTC+12, and greet the New Year among the first in the world. It was not always so: Kwajalein Atoll long lived a day behind and caught up with the rest of the country by simply dropping 21 August 1993 from its calendar. The big holidays here begin in church: at Christmas, church groups called jeptas sing and dance about island life — fishing, building homes, navigation — while church leaders pick the best.

Majuro is the capital: 64 islets around a vast lagoon, where the highest point is less than three metres above the sea. The city sees in the New Year at a big open-air party with local bands, food stalls and a shared countdown, and at midnight fireworks have often boomed over Uliga — though some years go without.

traditions.title: Christmas jeptas
traditions.text: At Christmas, church groups called jeptas sing and dance in Majuro’s churches, each in its own uniform. Their dances show fishing and navigation, and candies fly into the crowd.

traditions.title: An open-air block party
traditions.text: On 31 December Majuro gathers for a party with local bands, food stalls and a shared countdown. At midnight fireworks often boom over Uliga, though not every year.

traditions.title: A canoe on the lagoon
traditions.text: Islanders long sailed between atolls in proas, guided by the stars and stick charts. In Majuro canoes are still built today, young people learn to sail, and guests can ride across the lagoon.

meta.title: New Year in Majuro, Marshall Islands | Time2Fest
meta.description: Majuro, capital of the Marshall Islands, rings in 2027 at midnight UTC+12: an open-air party with bands and food stalls, a countdown and fireworks over Uliga.

MP.text:
The Northern Mariana Islands, a US territory in Micronesia, keep Chamorro Time, UTC+10, all year with no daylight saving. Midnight comes at 14:00 UTC, so together with Guam the islands are the first inhabited US land to see the New Year. Most of the celebrating happens on Saipan, in Garapan on the west coast: hotels lay on New Year’s Eve dinners, and one beachfront hotel throws a free countdown party open to all every year.

At midnight fireworks rise over that hotel’s garden and beach, and locals drive in to watch, filling Garapan’s car parks. On neighbouring Tinian the mayor’s office gathers people at the fiesta grounds every year: the party starts at seven in the evening and ends with a countdown and fireworks.

traditions.title: Countdown on Garapan’s beach
traditions.text: From nine in the evening until one in the morning a beachfront hotel in Garapan opens its garden and beach to everyone, no ticket needed: a live band plays, fire dancers perform and prizes are raffled.

traditions.title: Midnight fireworks in Garapan
traditions.text: At midnight fireworks rise over a hotel beach in Garapan. Local families come to watch too, so parking spots near the beach fill up early.

traditions.title: Tinian’s fiesta grounds
traditions.text: On neighbouring Tinian the mayor’s office gathers people at the fiesta grounds from seven in the evening every year, and leads the countdown under fireworks at midnight.

meta.title: New Year in the Northern Mariana Islands | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Northern Mariana Islands greet 2027 at 14:00 UTC. On Saipan, a free countdown party in Garapan, fireworks over the beach and a fiesta night on Tinian.

NC.text:
New Caledonia keeps UTC+11 all year, so midnight arrives here at 13:00 UTC, among the first in the world. Caledonians spend the night in many ways: quietly with family, at costume parties or at dressier evenings, with parties in town and out in the countryside alike. In the days before, shops sell out of ‘Bonne année’ balloons, headbands and confetti cannons.

In Nouméa, the capital, the heart of the night is the bays of Baie des Citrons and Anse Vata. Families claim a spot on the shore with mats and folding chairs, and at midnight a ‘concert of car horns’ rings out as cars drive round the bays, while the boldest dive into the sea. On the evening of 1 January the city gathers at Sainte-Marie bay: for years it meant fireworks, and in 2026 a sound and light show.

traditions.title: Round the bays, horns blaring
traditions.text: At midnight Nouméa strikes up its ‘concert of car horns’: cars with loud music drive round the bays, while families make the same tour on foot or with prams.

traditions.title: A midnight swim
traditions.text: The boldest greet the year in the water: the moment midnight strikes, they dive into the sea straight from the beach at Baie des Citrons or Anse Vata.

traditions.title: An evening on the shore
traditions.text: Families stake out a spot on the shore early with mats, folding tables and cool boxes, and pétanque players keep going late into the night.

meta.title: New Year in New Caledonia: Nouméa | Time2Fest
meta.description: New Caledonia greets 2027 at 13:00 UTC. In Nouméa families picnic on the bay beaches, car horns sound at midnight and the boldest dive in for a midnight swim.

NF.text:
Norfolk Island is an external territory of Australia in the middle of the Pacific, home to 2,188 people at the 2021 census. Many islanders descend from the Bounty mutineers and Tahitians who moved here from Pitcairn in 1856; their language, Norf'k, is official alongside English. The holiday season starts in November with Thanksgiving — Norfolk is the only place in Australia that keeps it — and before Christmas the main road of Burnt Pine glows with lights, with a Norfolk pine standing in for the Christmas tree.

Kingston is the island's capital, more a seat of government than a town. Its stone buildings from the 1830s — Government House, the Old Military Barracks, the Commissariat Store — are World Heritage. And from November to February families pitch tents under the pines around Emily Bay.

traditions.title: A pine for a Christmas tree
traditions.text: At the Christmas parade in Burnt Pine the main road is strung with lights, floats and Santa roll by, and a Norfolk pine — the tree on the island's flag — serves as the Christmas tree.

traditions.title: Summer in a tent under the pines
traditions.text: From November to February Norfolk families move into tents under the pines around Emily Bay or by Cemetery Beach — and still stay within a quarter of an hour of home.

traditions.title: Dishes that came from Pitcairn
traditions.text: Island cooking mixes British and Tahitian: try mudda, green-banana dumplings, and kumara pilhi, brought from Pitcairn by the settlers of 1856.

meta.title: New Year on Norfolk Island: Kingston | Time2Fest
meta.description: Norfolk Island greets 2027 at 12:00 UTC. Kingston's stone buildings from the 1830s are World Heritage, and in summer families camp under the pines by Emily Bay.

NR.text:
Naoero, formerly Nauru, is a raised coral island of 21 km² in the Pacific Ocean, home to 11,680 people at the 2021 census; in 2026 it officially took back its name in its own language. Midnight arrives here at 12:00 UTC, one of the first in the world. New Year's Day is a public holiday, and the festive month ends on 31 January with Independence Day: the country won its independence from Australia in 1968. The church is the heart of the community, and celebrations bring singing and the reigen circle dance.

Yaren is the de facto capital, since the country has no official one. Its one and a half square kilometres hold Parliament House, the airport, government offices and Moqua Well, an underground lake that was long the source of drinking water. Next door, in the neighbouring district, lies Buada Lagoon, a small rain-fed lake among coconut palms and gardens.

traditions.title: Holidays with the parish
traditions.text: In Naoero the church holds the community together: at the 2021 census a third of people belonged to the Nauru Congregational Church and another third were Catholic.

traditions.title: Reigen and the frigate bird
traditions.text: At celebrations people sing rhythmic songs and dance in a circle, the reigen. In the frigate bird dance, girls mime the bird in flight and landing.

traditions.title: From New Year to 31 January
traditions.text: New Year opens a festive January: on the 31st Naoero marks Independence Day, won in 1968 and the country's main national holiday.

meta.title: New Year in Naoero (Nauru): Yaren | Time2Fest
meta.description: Naoero meets 2027 among the first: midnight in Yaren comes at 12:00 UTC. The coral island sings and dances the reigen, and January closes with Independence Day.

TV.text:
Tuvalu keeps a single time zone, UTC+12, and greets the New Year — Tausaga Fou in Tuvaluan — among the first in the world. It is nine low islands and atolls whose highest point is just 4.6 metres above the sea, and most people belong to the Church of Tuvalu. So the big holidays begin with prayer: at Christmas all five churches of Funafuti come together to sing in Tuvaluan, and communities dance the fatele in traditional titi skirts.

Funafuti is the capital atoll: a narrow strip of land 20 to 400 metres wide around a vast lagoon, home to more than 6,600 people. The country's largest building is the three-storey Government Building in Vaiaku, and between flights the runway down the middle of the island becomes a volleyball court. Every evening the town pauses for a quarter of an hour of prayer.

traditions.title: Dance the fatele
traditions.text: The song starts in the maneapa, the community hall, and grows louder and faster until it stops dead. Young women dance in lines while the beat is kept on mats and empty cracker tins.

traditions.title: A fakaala feast
traditions.text: A big occasion calls for a fakaala, a feast in the maneapa with food served on trays woven from coconut fronds. Speeches and dancing follow the meal.

traditions.title: Wear a fou
traditions.text: After church Tuvaluans step out in their Sunday best, and women and men alike wear a fou, a wreath of tropical flowers. Put one on and wish your family a happy Tausaga Fou.

meta.title: New Year in Funafuti, Tuvalu | Time2Fest
meta.description: Funafuti, Tuvalu’s capital, welcomes 2027 at midnight UTC+12, among the first on Earth: prayer, the fatele dance, a feast in the maneapa and flower wreaths.

WF.text:
Wallis and Futuna keeps UTC+12, so midnight arrives here at 12:00 UTC — earlier than anywhere else in France, 11 hours ahead of Paris. People see in the new year in many ways: at home with family, at restaurants or in a crowd at a bar. On Futuna the party can belong to a whole village: in 2019 the young people of Ono laid on an evening for their parents, with traditional dances, modern music and cups of kava, and almost no alcohol.

On Wallis, home to the capital Mata-Utu, many families cross to the islets of the lagoon during the day on 31 December and wait for midnight there, by the water. Custom has its place too: in 2022 the New Year ceremonies on Wallis began with offerings to the king.

traditions.title: A night on a lagoon islet
traditions.text: Many Wallis families cross to an islet in the lagoon during the day on 31 December and greet midnight right by the water.

traditions.title: Kava with the whole village
traditions.text: On Futuna a whole village may see in the year together: the young people prepare food and dances for their parents, and cups of kava go round instead of alcohol.

traditions.title: Offerings to the king
traditions.text: Wallis still has a king, and custom is alive here: in 2022 the island’s New Year ceremonies began with offerings to him.

meta.title: New Year in Wallis and Futuna: Mata-Utu | Time2Fest
meta.description: Wallis and Futuna greets 2027 at 12:00 UTC, first in France. Around Mata-Utu families wait for midnight on lagoon islets, and Futuna villages party together.

PG.text:
Around 840 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea — more than in any other country — and over 95% of people call themselves Christian. Big holidays and family gatherings here come with a mumu: food wrapped in banana leaves and slow-cooked in an earth oven over hot stones. The country runs on two time zones: Bougainville sees midnight an hour earlier, the rest of the country at 14:00 UTC.

Port Moresby switches on its Christmas lights at Ela Beach in early December. The city commission holds a New Year's Eve party with live music on the same beach every year, and at midnight fireworks light up the capital. Even heavy rain on the last night of 2025 did not stop thousands of people from coming down to the sea.

traditions.title: A mumu for the whole family
traditions.text: For a big feast people dig a pit, line it with hot stones and slow-cook meat and vegetables wrapped in banana leaves. A mumu is made together — and eaten together.

traditions.title: Midnight at Ela Beach
traditions.text: In Port Moresby the last evening of the year is spent by the sea: music and comedy fill Ela Beach, and at midnight fireworks burst over the city.

traditions.title: A clean beach by morning
traditions.text: After the fireworks that welcomed 2025, young people in Port Moresby turned out to clean up Ela Beach, so the year began with a clean shore for everyone.

meta.title: New Year in Papua New Guinea: Port Moresby | Time2Fest
meta.description: Papua New Guinea greets 2027 at 14:00 UTC: Port Moresby gathers at Ela Beach for music and midnight fireworks, and families share a mumu from the earth oven.

RU.text:
In Russia, New Year is the main family holiday of winter. Trees are decorated at home and on city squares, and Ded Moroz (Grandfather Frost) and Snegurochka (the Snow Maiden) bring children their presents. The night is spent at a long festive table with Olivier salad, 'shuba' herring salad and pelmeni dumplings. Many families habitually watch the Soviet New Year comedies Carnival Night and The Irony of Fate that evening, and at midnight the Kremlin chimes ring out, followed by the anthem. Then come the New Year holidays, lasting until Orthodox Christmas on 7 January.

The chimes the whole country hears are on the Kremlin's Spasskaya Tower above Red Square. At the end of 2025 New Year fairs with hot chocolate and carousels ran near the square, the GUM ice rink opened for the twentieth time, and the country's main tree, a 100-year-old, 26-metre spruce, stood on Cathedral Square inside the Kremlin. On the night into 1 January 2026 the Moscow metro ran until morning, free of charge.

traditions.title: Tree and Ded Moroz
traditions.text: Decorate a tree at home: on New Year's Eve Ded Moroz and Snegurochka bring children their presents.

traditions.title: Olivier and 'shuba'
traditions.text: Set a long family table: Olivier salad, herring under a fur coat and pelmeni.

traditions.title: The Kremlin chimes
traditions.text: Greet midnight to the Kremlin chimes from the Spasskaya Tower, followed by the anthem.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Russia: Moscow | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Moscow, 21:00 UTC, Russia meets 2027 with the Kremlin chimes and the anthem, and at home with a tree, Ded Moroz and a bowl of Olivier salad.

SB.text:
Solomon Islands is six large islands and more than a thousand small ones, where 60–70 languages are spoken and Pijin is the shared tongue. Almost everyone is Christian, so the old year is seen out with prayer. On Simbo Island three villages celebrate together every year: after the watch night service, at midnight they set fire to a pyramid of dried coconut leaves and bamboo on the beach, followed by canoe races, dancing and choir contests. The whole country reaches midnight at 13:00 UTC.

Honiara, the capital on the northwest coast of Guadalcanal, is home to almost 130,000 people. Here the New Year arrives with countdown concerts: at the end of 2024 local bands One Tox and DMP shared hotel stages with reggae singer Quino, and the music went on until morning.

traditions.title: Fire at midnight
traditions.text: On Simbo, after the watch night service, a pyramid of coconut leaves and bamboo is burned on the beach. The tall flame at midnight sees off the old year.

traditions.title: Canoe races
traditions.text: Over the New Year days villages compete in canoe races, dancing and choir singing. At the end the host village hands the next New Year over to its neighbours.

traditions.title: A live-music countdown
traditions.text: In Honiara the last night of the year is spent at concerts: local bands play right up to midnight, the crowd counts down the seconds — and keeps dancing.

meta.title: New Year in Solomon Islands: Honiara | Time2Fest
meta.description: Solomon Islands greets 2027 at 13:00 UTC: Honiara counts down at live concerts, while Simbo Island lights a beach bonfire at midnight and races canoes.

KP.text:
In North Korea the New Year is welcomed on 1 January, a public holiday and day off since 1946. Many families spend it at home and clean the house beforehand. Later, by the lunar calendar, comes another holiday, Seollal, when people fly kites, spin tops and play the folk game yunnori.

In Pyongyang midnight is struck by the clock chimes of the Grand People’s Study House, and fireworks light up the city. Since 2013 fireworks have been launched over Kim Il Sung Square and over the Juche Tower on the opposite bank of the Taedong. Since 2022 the main concert and fireworks have been held at the May Day Stadium on an island in the river.

traditions.title: Chimes at midnight
traditions.text: At twelve sharp the clock of the Grand People’s Study House chimes in Pyongyang, and the new year begins.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the Taedong
traditions.text: Pyongyang residents gather on Kim Il Sung Square and the Taedong embankment. Since 2022 the main fireworks have risen over the May Day Stadium.

traditions.title: A day off at home
traditions.text: 1 January is a day off. Most families spend the first day of the year at home, with the house cleaned beforehand.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in North Korea: Pyongyang | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Pyongyang, 15:00 UTC, North Korea greets 2027 with the chimes of the Grand People’s Study House and fireworks over the Taedong River.

VU.text:
Vanuatu keeps UTC+11 all year, so midnight arrives here at 13:00 UTC, among the first in the world. The holidays come one after another: Christmas, Family Day on 26 December and New Year's Day on 1 January, all three days off. Many town dwellers head back to their home islands to be with family, and the islands celebrate more loudly than the towns: from 1 January groups go from village to village singing and dancing ‘Bonne année’, and on the east of Epi island such visitors are welcomed until 15 January.

In Port Vila, the capital, fireworks light up the town at midnight. Some raise a glass of champagne at a party, some go to a midnight church service, others see the year in at home with family. Some families pitch tents right on the beach and celebrate there for several days.

traditions.title: ‘Bonne année’ singing
traditions.text: From 1 January, groups on the islands visit neighbouring villages singing and dancing to see off the old year and welcome the new one. It is a long-standing tradition in Vanuatu.

traditions.title: Home to your island
traditions.text: Christmas, Family Day and New Year come back to back, so many people from Port Vila travel to their own island to celebrate with family.

traditions.title: A few days on the beach
traditions.text: Some families in Port Vila see the year in camping on the beach: swimming, playing beach volleyball, sharing meals and praying morning and evening.

meta.title: New Year in Vanuatu: Port Vila | Time2Fest
meta.description: Vanuatu welcomes 2027 at 13:00 UTC. Port Vila marks midnight with fireworks and church services, while island groups tour villages singing Bonne année.

BN.text:
Brunei is a sultanate where Islam is the state religion and Muslims make up about 80% of its nearly 460,000 people. Public Christmas celebrations have been banned here since 2015, while New Year's Day is a public holiday — and a double one: on 1 January 1984 Brunei became fully independent. On the first Friday of January, imams in mosques across the country urge the faithful to give thanks for the past year and become better people. The whole country reaches midnight at 16:00 UTC.

In Bandar Seri Begawan, as everywhere in Brunei, the New Year brings Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah's address, broadcast nationwide: he sums up the year, speaks about young people and jobs, and wishes a happy year to all Bruneians, even those abroad. And 2027 has been named Visit Brunei Year, coinciding with the Sultan's Diamond Jubilee.

traditions.title: A double holiday on 1 January
traditions.text: The first day of the year in Brunei is a holiday and also the anniversary of the 1984 Proclamation of Independence. So the new year begins as the country's birthday too.

traditions.title: The Sultan's address
traditions.text: On New Year's Day Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah gives an address — on peace, young people and the country's future — and wishes a happy year to all Bruneians, even those abroad.

traditions.title: Taking stock at the mosque
traditions.text: At the first Friday prayers of the year, imams across the country invite worshippers to look back on the past year, give thanks for it and resolve to become better.

meta.title: New Year in Brunei: Bandar Seri Begawan | Time2Fest
meta.description: Brunei greets 2027 at 16:00 UTC: 1 January is a double holiday here, New Year and Independence anniversary, marked by the Sultan's New Year address.

PW.text:
Palau lives in a single time zone, UTC+9. Two-thirds of its people live on Koror, so New Year's Eve mostly happens there, at parties in restaurants and festive venues in Koror and other states. Sources mention no big city fireworks at New Year: Palau's main fireworks boom on 1 October, Independence Day, at the Capitol. New Year's Day is a public holiday, easy to spend on the water among the Rock Islands, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The holidays here are above all about family: relatives cook together and gather around a table of Palauan staples such as taro, cassava, fish and pork, and count down to midnight together. Nearly eight in ten Palauans are Christian, so many go to church on New Year's Eve or New Year's Day. The capital, Ngerulmud, is the least-populous in the world: no one lives there permanently.

traditions.title: A quiet night in Koror
traditions.text: People see in the New Year at parties in restaurants and festive venues in Koror and other states. The night usually passes calmly, without big incidents.

traditions.title: A pledge in the passport
traditions.text: Every visitor to Palau signs the Palau Pledge, a promise to the islands’ children to protect their nature. Its text is stamped right into the passport.

traditions.title: New Year’s Day on the water
traditions.text: New Year’s Day is a day off, perfect for the Rock Islands. Hundreds of green mushroom-shaped islets stand in the lagoon between Koror and Peleliu.

meta.title: New Year in Ngerulmud, Palau | Time2Fest
meta.description: Palau rings in 2027 at midnight UTC+9: a quiet night of parties in Koror, the Capitol in Ngerulmud, the Palau Pledge in the passport and the Rock Islands.

TL.text:
Timor-Leste lives in a single time zone, UTC+9, and almost all of its people are Catholic, so the year-end holidays follow one another: Christmas, and on 31 December another public holiday, National Heroes Day. At midnight people count down the last seconds of the year, set off fireworks and party, and New Year's Day is a day off. In early 2024 the President thanked the people and the security forces for a calm Christmas and New Year.

The capital welcomed 2024 with a celebration at the State Palace and a speech by the President, and the night passed calmly. Above the bay, on Cape Fatucama, stands the 27-metre Cristo Rei statue on a globe — 570 steps lead up to it.

traditions.title: Countdown and fireworks
traditions.text: At midnight people count down the last seconds of the year, set off fireworks and party. New Year’s Day is a public holiday.

traditions.title: Heroes Day on 31 December
traditions.text: The last day of the year is a public holiday, National Heroes Day. It was on 31 December 1978 that Nicolau Lobato, the country’s first prime minister, was killed.

traditions.title: 570 steps to Cristo Rei
traditions.text: Some greet the first morning of the year on Cape Fatucama: 570 steps with 14 Stations of the Cross lead to the statue, with views of Dili Bay and Atauro Island.

meta.title: New Year in Dili, Timor-Leste | Time2Fest
meta.description: Timor-Leste rings in 2027 at midnight UTC+9: a countdown and fireworks in Dili, National Heroes Day on 31 December and 570 steps up to Cristo Rei.

AF.text:
In Afghanistan 1 January is not the start of the year: daily life runs on the Solar Hijri calendar, and the new year arrives with Nowruz on 21 March. After 2021 the authorities cancelled Nowruz as a public holiday, though they do not forbid celebrating it privately. Instead, many Afghans count 1 January as their birthday: when no one had recorded a birth, documents were given the date that is easiest to remember.

In Kabul 1 January is not a holiday, and in 2027 it falls on a Friday, the weekly day off. Midnight comes here at 19:30 UTC. Greetings that day travel by messenger: young people wish each other a happy 'shared' birthday.

traditions.title: Everyone's birthday
traditions.text: Many Afghans have 1 January written in their papers as their birthday. So greet your Afghan friends that day — for many it really is their day.

traditions.title: Yalda night with pomegranates
traditions.text: On the longest night of the year, around 21 December, Afghan families stay up late around the table. The fruit of the night is the pomegranate, and some celebrate in a restaurant.

traditions.title: Haft mewa for Nowruz
traditions.text: For Nowruz on 21 March people make haft mewa, seven dried fruits and nuts in their own syrup, and samanak, a sweet dish of sprouted wheat.

meta.title: New Year in Afghanistan: Kabul | Time2Fest
meta.description: Afghanistan reaches 2027 at 19:30 UTC: in Kabul 1 January is a Friday off, and for many Afghans it is also the birthday written in their documents.

BT.text:
In Bhutan 1 January is not a public holiday: the main New Year, Losar, follows the lunar calendar and in 2027 falls on 7 February. Early January is still festive, though — on 2 January 2027 the country has a day off for Nyilo, the winter solstice, after which the days grow longer. In parts of western Bhutan the new year begins with it, and it is marked with archery and feasting. The whole country reaches midnight at 18:00 UTC.

In Thimphu people spend New Year's Eve in different ways: the young go to clubs with dancing, karaoke and lucky draws, hotels hold dinners with live music, and many stay at home with parents and children. On Nyilo children go from house to house reciting lolay, wishes of plenty for every part of the homestead; in 2024 about 750 children greeted households this way in Thimphu.

traditions.title: Lolay from door to door
traditions.text: On Nyilo children visit homes reciting lolay, wishes of plenty for the house and every part of the homestead. Hosts give them food, and the children end the day with a picnic together.

traditions.title: Nyilo: the days turn
traditions.text: The winter solstice is a public holiday in Bhutan, falling on 2 January in 2027. The shortest day of the year is marked with archery and a generous feast.

traditions.title: A club night or home
traditions.text: On 31 December Thimphu's clubs fill up for dancing, karaoke and lucky draws, and bars have live music. Others greet midnight at home over a family dinner.

meta.title: New Year in Bhutan: Thimphu | Time2Fest
meta.description: Bhutan reaches 2027 at 18:00 UTC: Thimphu spends the night in clubs or at home with family, and on 2 January, Nyilo, children go door to door with wishes.

CC.text:
On the Cocos (Keeling) Islands 1 January is a public holiday, as everywhere in Australia, but it is hardly a big celebration here. Most of the nearly six hundred islanders are Cocos Malays, Sunni Muslims, and their main days of the year follow the Islamic calendar: Hari Raya Puasa at the end of Ramadan and Hari Raya Haji. And on 6 April the islands mark their own Act of Self Determination Day.

The new year arrives here at 17:30 UTC, on a warm night: even after dark it rarely drops below 24 °C, and the lagoon stays around 26 °C. On 1 January the ferry between West Island and Home Island does not run — it never sails on public holidays.

traditions.title: A barbecue by a pondok
traditions.text: Cocos Malays keep pondoks — weekend shacks on the larger islets of the atoll. They take a barbecue and a fishing line there and spend the evening by the lagoon: even at night it rarely drops below 24 °C.

traditions.title: New Year's Day without a ferry
traditions.text: 1 January is a public holiday, and the ferry between West Island and Home Island does not run, just as on Sundays. So everyone spends the first day of the year on their own island.

traditions.title: Forgiveness at Hari Raya
traditions.text: Home Island's biggest celebration is Hari Raya Puasa after Ramadan (around 9 March in 2027). In the morning families in matching outfits visit their relatives' graves and ask one another's forgiveness for the past year's wrongs.

meta.title: New Year on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands greet 2027 at 17:30 UTC on a warm night by the lagoon. 1 January is a ferry-free holiday; the Malay big day is Hari Raya.

LA.text:
The main New Year in Laos is Pi Mai Lao in mid-April: during the 14–16 April holiday people wash Buddha images, splash one another with water, the young first pouring it on their elders, and build sand stupas for the temples. Yet 1 January is a public holiday too, and the night before it is spent at home, in villages, at offices and in big public squares across the country. Midnight in Laos comes at 17:00 UTC.

In Vientiane the heart of the night is the park around the Patuxai arch. Folk music plays, Lao motifs are projected onto the monument's arches, and when the countdown hits zero fireworks burst above Patuxai. According to the Vientiane Times, more than 100,000 people came for the 2026 countdown, and on the night into 2025 the crowd danced the lamvong, freshly inscribed by UNESCO as heritage of humanity.

traditions.title: Countdown at Patuxai
traditions.text: At midnight the park around the Patuxai arch counts down to zero, Lao motifs light up the monument and fireworks burst above it. On the night into 2025 Laos saw its first drone show, with That Luang stupa in the sky.

traditions.title: The lamvong dance
traditions.text: In December 2024 UNESCO inscribed the Lao lamvong dance as intangible heritage of humanity, and on New Year's Eve Patuxai Park saw more than eight of its styles danced to folk music.

traditions.title: A second New Year in April
traditions.text: At Pi Mai Lao, on 14–16 April, people wash Buddha images, pour water over their elders and build sand stupas to offer to the monks at the temple.

meta.title: New Year in Laos: Vientiane | Time2Fest
meta.description: Laos greets 2027 at 17:00 UTC: Vientiane counts down at the Patuxai arch with fireworks and Lao motifs on the monument, while Pi Mai waits until April.

MM.text:
Myanmar has two New Years. The traditional one is Thingyan in April, a water festival when people drench each other to wash away the bad luck of the old year; in 2027 its holiday runs from 10 to 18 April. Until 2012 the night of 1 January was mostly spent at home or in hotels, and in 2018 the first day of the year became a public holiday for the first time. The whole country reaches midnight at 17:30 UTC.

In Yangon, the largest city, the first public countdown took place on 31 December 2012 at the Myoma grounds: a concert, a big screen and fireworks, with about 90,000 people according to the organisers. In 2022 the city authorities lifted the curfew for one night for a countdown with fireworks and music at People's Park, and did so again on 31 December 2023.

traditions.title: A water New Year in April
traditions.text: During Thingyan the young wash the hair of their elders as a sign of respect, people release fish and birds, and rice balls filled with palm sugar are cooked in the streets.

traditions.title: A countdown with fireworks
traditions.text: Yangon's first public countdown with a concert and fireworks took place on 31 December 2012, and in 2022 one was held at People's Park with music and fireworks.

traditions.title: A ceremony at Shwedagon
traditions.text: On 1 January a Buddhist New Year's Day ceremony is held at Shwedagon Pagoda: in 2018 some 18,000 monks and nuns gathered for it.

meta.title: New Year in Myanmar: Yangon | Time2Fest
meta.description: Myanmar greets 2027 at 17:30 UTC: Yangon meets midnight with a countdown and fireworks, and on 1 January a Buddhist ceremony is held at Shwedagon Pagoda.

MO.text:
Macau, under Portuguese rule for 442 years, welcomes the New Year twice. 1 January is a holiday, but the biggest festival is Lunar New Year: the eve and the first three days are off, and in 2027 it falls on 6 February. On the first day a 238-metre golden dragon with eighteen lions parades from the Ruins of St. Paul's to Senado Square, where firecrackers are lit, and on later days fireworks rise opposite Macau Tower.

The night of 31 December means free countdown concerts by Sai Van Lake and at the Taipa Houses, where the Tuna Macaense ensemble sings alongside Filipino, Vietnamese and Myanmar community groups. The city concerts have no fireworks, but at midnight the Cotai resorts have fired 8 minutes of them. On New Year's Eve 2023 more than 175,000 visitors came to Macau, a post-pandemic record.

traditions.title: Dragon and firecrackers
traditions.text: The main festival is Lunar New Year, on 6 February in 2027. On the first day a 238-metre golden dragon with eighteen lions parades from the Ruins of St. Paul's to Senado Square, where firecrackers are lit.

traditions.title: Count down at an open-air gig
traditions.text: The city stages two free concerts: by Sai Van Lake from 22:00 to 00:10, and at the Taipa Houses, with the Tuna Macaense ensemble and community dance groups.

traditions.title: Fireworks over Cotai
