meta.description: Rwanda greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC with evening church services, fireworks at exactly midnight by the Kigali Convention Centre and a family feast with gifts.

LB.text:
In Lebanon 1 January is a public holiday, and the holidays come one after another: Christmas on 25 December, New Year, and on 6 January Armenians mark their own Christmas. New Year's Eve is above all a dinner with family and friends, with tabbouleh, hummus and kibbeh on the table. Others head to restaurants and clubs, the party often lasts until sunrise, and fireworks go up all night. At the end of 2025 hotels in Beirut and at the ski resorts were 80–100% full.

Beirut greets the year with concerts and parties, so tables and tickets go early. In December trees are lit downtown, with holiday markets and concerts. And in 2018 National Geographic put Beirut's night among the world's top ten: thousands gathered in Nejmeh Square by the 1933 clock tower, and fireworks went up around midnight.

traditions.title: Dinner with family
traditions.text: New Year in Lebanon starts at the table with family and friends: tabbouleh, hummus, kibbeh and other Lebanese dishes.

traditions.title: A night until dawn
traditions.text: Restaurants, clubs and concerts go on until morning; for the night of 2023/24 about 750 parties were planned nationwide. Tables are booked early.

traditions.title: Markets and lights
traditions.text: In December the towns glow with trees: markets and concerts in downtown Beirut, festivities by the old port of Byblos, and Batroun's streets strung with lights.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Lebanon: Beirut | Time2Fest
meta.description: Lebanon greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: a family dinner of tabbouleh and kibbeh, Beirut's concerts and clubs until sunrise, and festive lights in Byblos and Batroun.

LS.text:
In Lesotho 1 January is a public holiday, even though the Basotho's own New Year, Selemo sa Basotho, is marked in August, when nature wakes after winter. December and January are the season of homecomings: Basotho who work in South Africa travel home for Christmas and New Year. They are welcomed with warmth and good food, families gather, and children wait eagerly for the gifts they bring.

In December 2025 Maseru's Main Circle lit up with festive lights and colourful illuminated fountains, and families and groups of friends came to watch. For 31 December the government announced a national celebration on the renewed Makoanyane Square, from 18:00 right up to midnight.

traditions.title: Home for the holidays
traditions.text: For Christmas and New Year, Basotho working in South Africa come home to their families. Good food awaits them, and children wait for gifts.

traditions.title: Lights on the Main Circle
traditions.text: In December 2025 the roundabout in central Maseru was decked with festive lights and illuminated fountains. In the evening families and friends gather here.

traditions.title: Until midnight on the square
traditions.text: For 31 December 2025 the government announced a national celebration on Makoanyane Square in Maseru, from 18:00 until midnight. The 2027 programme will be announced closer to the date.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Lesotho: Maseru | Time2Fest
meta.description: Lesotho greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: Basotho working in South Africa head home to family, and Maseru glows with Main Circle lights before midnight.

SS.text:
In South Sudan the New Year comes a week after Christmas, so the end of December is one long festive season: 25 and 26 December and 1 January are public holidays. For many, the heart of New Year's night is church: the year is seen off with prayer at a night service. In their New Year messages, church leaders call for the coming year to be one of peace, love and integrity.

Juba stands on the White Nile. There is no city fireworks show at midnight: police have banned fireworks and asked people to welcome the year calmly. Officers are posted at churches and on the streets that night so the service and the way home stay safe. And the capital's advice: if you go out as a group, one person stays sober and drives the others home.

traditions.title: A night service at church
traditions.text: Many spend the last hours of the year at a night service: in Juba, police are posted at churches that night so it all passes peacefully.

traditions.title: A wish for peace
traditions.text: Church New Year messages call for prayer for a year of peace, love and integrity — add that wish to your own greetings.

traditions.title: One sober driver
traditions.text: Groups going out agree who stays sober that night and drives everyone home — that was Juba's advice before the New Year.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in South Sudan: Juba | Time2Fest
meta.description: South Sudan greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: night services in Juba's churches, prayers for a peaceful year and a quiet night without fireworks on the White Nile.

ZA.text:
In South Africa the New Year arrives at the height of summer, and 1 January is a public holiday. On the evening of 31 December people hold a braai, grilling meat over an open fire, and at midnight fireworks go up all over the country. In Cape Town the party on the V&A Waterfront is free, from 6 pm until 1 am, and at the stroke of midnight a five-minute fireworks show lights up the harbour. Yet Cape Town's biggest celebration comes on 2 January, the «Second New Year»: thousands of minstrels in bright costumes and with umbrellas march through the city to the beat of the ghoema drum. The day goes back to the time of slavery, when enslaved people were given 2 January off.

In Johannesburg fireworks are allowed only from 11 pm to 1 am, so the sky over the city flares up right around midnight. And for the arrival of 2025, the 269-metre Hillbrow Tower lit up at midnight with the words «Happy New Year».

traditions.title: Fireworks over the harbour
traditions.text: In Cape Town the party on the V&A Waterfront is free, and at midnight fireworks light up the harbour for five minutes.

traditions.title: A braai under the sky
traditions.text: New Year's Eve falls in midsummer and often means a braai, meat grilled over a fire, with fireworks flaring across the country at midnight.

traditions.title: The Second New Year
traditions.text: On 2 January Cape Town holds its carnival: up to 13,000 minstrels in bright costumes, with umbrellas and the ghoema drum.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in South Africa: Johannesburg | Time2Fest
meta.description: South Africa greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC with midsummer braais, a midnight fireworks show over Cape Town's harbour and the Second New Year carnival on 2 January.

BJ.text:
Firecrackers are off limits on New Year's Eve in Benin: a 2022 decree bans them, and the police ask people to celebrate without excess. So for many the night is spent in church, with thanksgiving masses, prayers and vigils running through midnight, and some stay until morning to place the new year in God's hands. Before the holiday yards are swept and houses tidied, so the year begins clean and with the family together. Early in January Ouidah draws thousands to Vodun Days, a festival of Vodun culture.

Light arches, glittering trees and lanterns dress the squares and crossroads of Porto-Novo and neighbouring Cotonou for the holidays. From the evening of 1 January, a public holiday, families come to stroll, picnic on the grass and take photos under the lights.

traditions.title: A night in church
traditions.text: Cotonou's churches are packed on 31 December: thanksgiving masses and night vigils run through midnight, and some people pray until morning.

traditions.title: A clean home for the year
traditions.text: Yards are swept, houses tidied and dishes washed, so the year begins clean, calm and with the family together.

traditions.title: Kaléta masks
traditions.text: All through December children in masks and costumes of rags and raffia dance through Cotonou's streets to drums and are given sweets or coins for it.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Benin: Porto-Novo | Time2Fest
meta.description: Benin greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with church vigils through the night, a freshly swept home and light arches on the squares of Porto-Novo and Cotonou.

CF.text:
In the Central African Republic New Year's Eve is spent above all with family and in church: many go to a night service to thank God for the year they have lived through, while others head for kermesses and dancing. On the table there is chicken, gnetum (koko leaves), bushmeat and home-made drinks; elders in their grand boubous recall past celebrations, and everyone wishes each other good health. The country has lived with armed conflict since 2012, so gunfire and firecrackers are banned that night, and for the arrival of 2026 even the traditional 21 cannon shots were called off.

In Bangui hairdressers and tailors work until the last minute before the holiday, and the KM5 market buzzes with shoppers. At midnight the faithful gather in Notre-Dame Cathedral, and on 1 January the streets are full of people: some celebrate at home, others with friends in bars.

traditions.title: Chicken for the feast
traditions.text: Chicken is the main New Year dish in Bangui: it is bought at the market the day before and served with gnetum, bushmeat and home-made drinks.

traditions.title: A night service of thanks
traditions.text: On 31 December many people go to church to thank God for the year gone by; Notre-Dame Cathedral in Bangui holds a New Year's Eve mass.

traditions.title: A fire in the courtyard
traditions.text: Some families light a fire in the courtyard in the evening: around it people tell stories, sing old village songs and wish each other good health.

meta.title: New Year in the Central African Republic | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Central African Republic greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: Bangui goes to mass at Notre-Dame, serves chicken with gnetum and fills the streets on 1 January.

SD.text:
In Sudan the first day of the year is a double celebration: the country became independent on 1 January 1956, so New Year's Day is also Independence Day and a public holiday. That day Prime Minister Ismail al-Azhari raised the Sudanese flag for the first time. The holiday season is long: Christmas on 25 December and Coptic Christmas on 7 January are days off too. In 2019 Christmas bells rang in Khartoum for the first time in ten years, and Christians and Muslims celebrated together.

In Khartoum, on 1 January 2020, independence and the new year were celebrated in Freedom Square. Since April 2023 Sudan has been at war. On 1 January 2026 the capital marked 70 years of independence with a Youth Sports Festival: races for adults and children and a cycling race through the city's streets became the first large event since the war began.

traditions.title: New Year and independence
traditions.text: Midnight brings not only a new year but also Independence Day, a public holiday that recalls 1 January 1956.

traditions.title: Christmas days to 7 January
traditions.text: Both 25 December and 7 January, Coptic Christmas, are days off; in 2019 Christians and Muslims celebrated Christmas together in Khartoum.

traditions.title: A sporting 1 January
traditions.text: In 2026 Khartoum greeted the independence anniversary with races for adults and children and a cycling race through its streets.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Sudan: Khartoum | Time2Fest
meta.description: Sudan greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC, and here the first day of the year is also Independence Day, marking 1956. Holidays run from Christmas to Coptic 7 January.

SZ.text:
In Eswatini the night into 1 January is called the «crossover» — the step into the new year — and New Year's Day itself is a public holiday. Many people greet midnight in church or at a gospel concert: night services run from the evening into the first hours of the year, and at midnight people pray and sing. For years the biggest gospel crossovers have filled the Mavuso Trade Fair in Manzini, from 6 pm until 6 am. The New Year also falls in the season of Incwala, the country's most important ceremony, devoted to kingship and the first fruits.

In Mbabane, the crossover into 2025 brought gospel stars to Prince of Wales Stadium, with ticket money going to charity. Fireworks in Eswatini are private and brief: Manzini allowed them only from 23:30 to 01:30.

traditions.title: A night service
traditions.text: On 31 December churches gather believers for crossover services from 7 pm into the first hours of the new year, greeting midnight with prayer and song.

traditions.title: Gospel until dawn
traditions.text: The big gospel crossover at Mavuso runs from 6 pm to 6 am: singing, dancing, prayer and thanks for the year gone by.

traditions.title: A night on four stages
traditions.text: Club crossovers in Manzini run from afternoon to morning, with amapiano, deep house, hip hop and gospel on separate stages.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Eswatini: Mbabane | Time2Fest
meta.description: Eswatini crosses into 2027 at 22:00 UTC with night church services, a gospel crossover until dawn at Mavuso, brief private fireworks and the Incwala season.

ZM.text:
In Zambia 1 January is a public holiday, and for many people New Year's Eve begins in church. Churches hold crossovers, night services of song and prayer that run through midnight; in charismatic churches they often end with the announcement of the theme the congregation carries into the new year. On many family tables there is chicken with rice: it is eaten at Christmas and on New Year's Day by long tradition, so in December poultry farmers can barely keep up with orders.

In Lusaka fireworks crack and car horns sound at midnight, and the bars are full of music. Thousands see the year in at the Showgrounds, where DJs, a countdown and fireworks have been an annual fixture for more than eight years. For the arrival of 2025 fireworks also lit up the sky over the city centre.

traditions.title: A crossover night
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December many Zambians head to church for a crossover, a night service of song and prayer that runs through midnight and ends in the new year.

traditions.title: Chicken with rice
traditions.text: On New Year's Day many families serve chicken with rice, and eggs go into salads, cakes and pastries — a holiday table handed down for generations.

traditions.title: Countdown at the Showgrounds
traditions.text: Lusaka's biggest New Year party is at the Showgrounds: DJs, a countdown and fireworks at midnight, while car horns sound across the city.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Zambia: Lusaka | Time2Fest
meta.description: Zambia greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC with crossover church services through the night, chicken and rice at home and a fireworks countdown at the Lusaka Showgrounds.

ZW.text:
In Zimbabwe 1 January is a public holiday, and 31 December is a day of errands: people stock up on food, drinks and firecrackers. In the evening some head to church for a crossover — an all-night service where the theme of the new year is unveiled around midnight, followed by prayer into the early hours. Others see the year in with family and friends. And no celebration is complete without rice and chicken, the favourite dish of every Zimbabwean feast, from weddings to Christmas.

In Harare thousands spill into the streets and entertainment spots for live music and street food, and at midnight the sky bursts with fireworks. On 1 January the Harare International Conference Centre fills with thousands for the gospel concert A Night of Thanksgiving; for 2026 its overnight session began as early as 11 pm.

traditions.title: A night at crossover
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December many go to church for a crossover: the theme of the new year is unveiled around midnight, and prayer goes on into the early hours.

traditions.title: Rice and chicken
traditions.text: Rice and chicken is the dish no Zimbabwean celebration goes without — from weddings and graduations to Christmas.

traditions.title: Harare's music night
traditions.text: Harare sees the year in on the streets with live music and fireworks, and on 1 January thousands gather for the gospel concert A Night of Thanksgiving.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Zimbabwe: Harare | Time2Fest
meta.description: Zimbabwe welcomes 2027 at 22:00 UTC with all-night crossover services, rice and chicken on the table, and live music and fireworks across the streets of Harare.

CM.text:
Cameroon's churches call the night into 1 January the 'crossover': services named 'Cross over night' or 'Breakthrough night' run through midnight, and Catholics go to the crossing mass to give thanks and pray for the year ahead. Markets buzz before the holiday, because the table needs nnam ngon: ground pumpkin seeds with meat or smoked fish, wrapped in banana leaves, simmered for two or three hours and served with cassava sticks. Children get new clothes and toys, often little cars and dolls.

Around ten in the evening Yaoundé heads out in every direction: to churches, restaurants and clubs, to the big junctions or to the family table. People come dressed in white to the night service at Glory of Christ Chapel, and Our Lady of Victories Cathedral holds a special mass. At midnight 'Happy New Year!' rings out everywhere, and neighbours' fireworks light up the sky.

traditions.title: Nnam ngon for the feast
traditions.text: Ground pumpkin seeds with meat or smoked fish are wrapped in banana leaves and simmered for two or three hours, then eaten with cassava sticks.

traditions.title: A crossover service
traditions.text: On 31 December churches gather people from ten in the evening into the first hours of the new year; some night services ask everyone to wear white.

traditions.title: Midnight at the junction
traditions.text: Yaoundé's big junctions, bars and restaurants fill with music and dancing before midnight, and at the first minute of the year everyone trades greetings.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Cameroon: Yaoundé | Time2Fest
meta.description: Cameroon reaches 2027 at 23:00 UTC with crossover church services, nnam ngon slow-cooked in banana leaves and 'Happy New Year!' at Yaoundé's junctions.

AO.text:
Sixty-five night prayer vigils and 126 parties: that is how many New Year gatherings Luanda alone authorised for the arrival of 2026, so some people see the year out in church and others dance until morning. At midnight fireworks go up across Angola, and 1 January is a public holiday. On the festive table there is calulu, dried fish with vegetables, or feijoada, a bean and meat stew, and glasses are raised with sparkling wine.

Luanda starts celebrating while it is still light: at six in the evening the 10 km São Silvestre race, run since 1954, sets off from Largo da Mutamba. The course follows the Marginal along the bay, and at Praia da Nicha midnight was greeted with a free concert and fireworks.

traditions.title: São Silvestre race at 18:00
traditions.text: Angola's biggest athletics event of the year: ten kilometres from Largo da Mutamba along the Marginal to the stadium. In 2022, 2,241 runners signed up.

traditions.title: Church vigil or party
traditions.text: Midnight here is met both at night prayer vigils and at parties: for the arrival of 2026, Luanda authorised 65 vigils and 126 parties.

traditions.title: Calulu and a sparkling toast
traditions.text: Calulu, dried fish stewed with vegetables, or a hearty feijoada of beans and meat. At midnight the glasses are filled with sparkling wine.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Angola: Luanda | Time2Fest
meta.description: Angola meets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: Luanda runs the São Silvestre race along the Marginal at dusk, then midnight fireworks, calulu and sparkling wine.

DZ.text:
On 31 December queues form outside the pastry shops of Algiers as people collect their festive bûche, a log cake in lemon, chocolate or mocha. A New Year dinner is hardly complete without one: families or friends gather round a generous table, and groups of friends take turns hosting, each bringing something along. Some head for the desert for the holidays — to the oasis of Taghit, to Djanet or Tamanrasset. Others do not celebrate 31 December at all, as they do not see it as their holiday. New Year’s Day is a public holiday.

Twelve days later comes another New Year: Amazigh Yennayer, also a public holiday since 2018. For the imensi n yennayer dinner, couscous is cooked with chicken or meat, and everyone must eat their fill so the year will be one of plenty. The youngest child in the family is gently showered with “treize”, a mix of sweets, chocolate and nuts.

traditions.title: A bûche for the table
traditions.text: Log cakes are ordered early: on 31 December the pastry shops have long queues, and an Algerian New Year dinner is hardly complete without a bûche.

traditions.title: Holidays in an oasis
traditions.text: Many see in the year among the sand dunes: every year-end thousands of people travel to Taghit, Djanet and Tamanrasset.

traditions.title: Couscous for Yennayer
traditions.text: On 12 January cook couscous for the imensi n yennayer dinner, eat your fill and shower the youngest in the family with sweets and nuts for a year of plenty.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Algeria: Algiers | Time2Fest
meta.description: Algeria greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with queues for the festive bûche, family dinners or a night in the Taghit oasis, and Yennayer couscous on 12 January.

BA.text:
Skiing at midnight is no joke on Jahorina: on New Year's Eve the resort opens its slopes from 22:00 to 02:00, and up on the summit, by the Olimp bar, an open-air party welcomes skiers and anyone who came up without skis. Down in the bigger cities of Bosnia and Herzegovina the streets are decorated, squares fill with concerts and fireworks, and restaurants, cafés and hotels throw New Year's parties. The 1st and 2nd of January are days off, and in Republika Srpska the Orthodox New Year is marked again on 14 January.

Two years running, the peak of Sarajevo's New Year's night came with one song — Kemal Monteno's "Sarajevo, ljubavi moja": Severina led the city into 2025 with it, and a year later Jelena Rozga sang it. That night about 64,000 people gathered on the Vrbanja plateau by Sarajevo City Center, and trumpet and rock bands play across town until morning.

traditions.title: Skiing till 2 a.m.
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve Jahorina's slopes stay open from 22:00 to 02:00, and midnight is met on the summit at the party by the Olimp bar.

traditions.title: "Sarajevo, ljubavi moja"
traditions.text: Sarajevo entered the new year with Kemal Monteno's song two years running — 2025 and 2026. Learn the chorus and sing along.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the Neretva
traditions.text: Mostar welcomed 2025 with fireworks over the city on the Neretva and a concert; on 1 January Prljavo kazalište kept the party going.

meta.title: New Year in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Sarajevo | Time2Fest
meta.description: Midnight skiing on Jahorina, a big concert in Sarajevo and "Sarajevo, ljubavi moja": Bosnia and Herzegovina greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC and parties till dawn.

LI.text:
“A good new year, a long life, good health and a place in heaven” — with this old wish children in Liechtenstein greet the grown-ups at New Year, and are thanked with coins. The New Year days here belong to one long season from Christmas to Epiphany: on 6 January the star singers walk the streets, and the children give everything they collect to an aid project.

Vaduz meets midnight on an ice rink in the middle of town: on New Year’s Eve the rink on the Rathausplatz stays open until 1 am with free entry. Private fireworks are tolerated only around midnight and until 1 am — after that, night rest falls across the country. Liechtenstein saves its big fireworks for 15 August, the national holiday by Vaduz Castle.

traditions.title: A wish for a coin
traditions.text: By old custom, children wish the grown-ups a good new year, a long life, good health and a place in heaven — and get coins for it.

traditions.title: Skating until 1 am
traditions.text: On New Year’s Eve the Vaduz on Ice rink on the Rathausplatz stays open until 1 am with free entry, next to an open-air disco.

traditions.title: Fireworks only at midnight
traditions.text: In Liechtenstein fireworks go up around midnight and no later than 1 am, then night rest begins. Towns suggest quiet fountains instead of loud bangers.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Liechtenstein: Vaduz | Time2Fest
meta.description: Liechtenstein greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: skating on the Vaduz Rathausplatz until 1 am, fireworks around midnight and an old children's wish paid in coins.

NE.text:
Niger welcomes the new year twice: the Muslim one in the month of Muharram, by the lunar calendar, while the Gregorian 1 January is a public holiday. Everyone spends the night before it in their own way. Some invite friends for dinner at home, others sit in their fada — a circle of friends who meet over tea, and on this night over grilled brochettes too. Some believers don't mark the holiday at all.

At midnight Niamey bursts into car horns: motorcades of motorbikes and cars circle the big roundabouts to the crackle of firecrackers, and young people on Place Anoutab launch their own fireworks. The street party is short — afterwards some head home, others go on to the nightclubs.

traditions.title: A night at the fada
traditions.text: A fada is a circle of friends who meet to talk over tea. On New Year's Eve the tea comes with brochettes — grilled meat on skewers.

traditions.title: Horns at the roundabouts
traditions.text: At midnight motorbikes and cars drive in convoys round Niamey's big roundabouts — Mali Béro, Martyrs, Liberté — honking and setting off firecrackers.

traditions.title: Dinner with friends at home
traditions.text: Not everyone takes to the streets: many invite friends for a New Year dinner at home — sometimes as many as fifty guests.

meta.title: New Year in Niger: Niamey | Time2Fest
meta.description: Niger greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: Niamey honks in motorcades round its big roundabouts, fadas gather over tea and brochettes, and friends share dinner at home.

LU.text:
“All the best in the new year — and a wig of goat's hair, and seven lice on one hair”: that is the full Luxembourgish New Year rhyme, though people usually say only the first half, “Alles Guddes am neie Joer”. Most celebrate midnight at home with family or friends, and the invitation may arrive as early as autumn. The table holds pâté, foie gras, fondue or oysters, and just before the stroke of twelve the hosts take a bottle of crémant, the local sparkling wine, out of the fridge. On 1 January, a public holiday, people sleep in and then visit relatives, while children receive a “neit Jäerchen” — sweets or a little money — from grandparents and godparents.

The capital holds no fireworks display, and firecrackers are banned in the city, so the night plays out in bars, clubs and at balls. Only some municipalities allow fireworks — and only in a short window around midnight.

traditions.title: Crémant at midnight
traditions.text: At midnight Luxembourgers clink glasses of crémant, the local sparkling wine, while children get something alcohol-free. Raise a glass with them.

traditions.title: The goat-hair wig wish
traditions.text: At midnight people wish “Alles Guddes am neie Joer”, and those in the know finish the rhyme: “an eng Paréck mat Geessenhoer, a siwe Lais op engem Hoer”.

traditions.title: A neit Jäerchen for kids
traditions.text: On 1 January people sleep in and visit aunts and uncles, and children get a neit Jäerchen — a “little new year” of sweets or a few coins — from grandparents and godparents.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Luxembourg | Time2Fest
meta.description: Luxembourg greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with crémant at midnight among friends, a rhyme about a goat-hair wig and family visits with a neit Jäerchen on 1 January.

ME.text:
For a quarter of a century Budva has greeted the New Year on the square in front of its Old Town walls: in 2024 the free celebration was held for the 25th time, and it runs over several evenings. At midnight on 31 December fireworks burst over the Old Town, and on 1 January a New Year concert plays on the square. Kotor answers with its “Rock New Year”: in 1997 it held the first open-air New Year concert in Montenegro. In Tivat the last seconds are counted by the Porto Montenegro marina, with fireworks over the berths.

Another night of fire comes on 6 January, Badnji dan: men bring oak branches from the forest, and large bonfires burn by the churches. At Christmas the table holds priganice and buns with homemade cheese and pršut, and on the night of 14 January many people greet the New Year a second time — by the old calendar.

traditions.title: Fireworks over Budva’s walls
traditions.text: At midnight fireworks burst over Budva’s Old Town, and concerts on the main square go on for several evenings in a row — seven of them for the arrival of 2026.

traditions.title: Rock New Year in Kotor
traditions.text: On the main square of Kotor’s Old Town the New Year arrives with a rock concert by bands from across the former Yugoslavia; the first open-air show of this kind took place in 1997.

traditions.title: Badnji dan bonfires
traditions.text: On 6 January men bring oak branches from the forest and large bonfires burn by the churches; the next day, at Christmas, families fry priganice.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Montenegro: Podgorica | Time2Fest
meta.description: Montenegro greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: fireworks over Budva’s walls, rock on Kotor’s main square, a countdown at Tivat’s marina, a second New Year on 14 January.

MT.text:
White lime on the doorstep: that is how the Maltese once greeted the new year, sprinkling their thresholds as a sign of purity and a fresh start, while on 1 January children went round their relatives collecting l-istrina, coins and treats. These customs have all but gone, but the family lunch on New Year's Day remains; an old belief says that whoever eats cabbage that day will groan all year. Over the winter holidays people brew imbuljuta, a hot drink of cocoa, chestnuts, cloves and citrus peel. The young, meanwhile, see in midnight at clubs and dance parties.

The country's big night is in Valletta: since 2010 the countdown has taken place in St George's Square with an open-air concert. Last time, by the government's estimate, about 70,000 people came, and at midnight a 25-minute fireworks display, the largest in the event's history, lit up the Grand Harbour. Across the harbour, on the Cospicua waterfront, another concert was playing.

traditions.title: Fireworks over Grand Harbour
traditions.text: At midnight, the Maltese take their places above the Grand Harbour, on the bastions and the waterfront: last year the fireworks over it lasted 25 minutes.

traditions.title: Chestnut imbuljuta
traditions.text: Brew a hot imbuljuta of cocoa, chestnuts, cloves and citrus peel, the Maltese drink of the winter holidays.

traditions.title: New Year's Day lunch
traditions.text: Gather the family at the table on 1 January and leave out the cabbage: an old Maltese belief says whoever eats it that day will groan all year.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Malta: Valletta | Time2Fest
meta.description: Malta greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with an open-air concert in St George's Square, Valletta, fireworks over the Grand Harbour and hot chestnut imbuljuta.

HR.text:
Croatia starts counting down at noon: Zagreb and Ogulin hold a midday “midnight” for children, and in Fužine and Novi Vinodolski the noon countdown draws thousands. In the evening guests are greeted with a glass of rakija, and the table holds suckling pig or lamb, sarma made with sauerkraut and a “French salad” that lasts for days. At midnight comes a glass of sparkling wine, ideally from the Plešivica vineyards.

At night Zagreb gathers on Ban Jelačić Square: an open-air concert, with the mayor counting down the last seconds along with everyone. On the coast the main stage is Stradun in Dubrovnik, where midnight brings the traditional fireworks over the Old Town. And in Osijek people have been seeing off the old year with a swim in the Drava for more than thirty years.

traditions.title: Midnight at noon
traditions.text: On 31 December, children in Zagreb and Ogulin gather for a party before noon: there the new year is greeted symbolically at twelve o'clock in the day.

traditions.title: Pig, sarma and salad
traditions.text: Set the table the Croatian way: suckling pig or lamb, sarma in sauerkraut leaves and a “French salad” big enough to last for days.

traditions.title: Fireworks over Stradun
traditions.text: At midnight, Dubrovnik gathers on Stradun: after the open-air concert the traditional New Year fireworks light up the Old Town.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Croatia: Zagreb | Time2Fest
meta.description: Croatia greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with a noon countdown for kids, suckling pig and sarma, a concert in Zagreb and fireworks over Stradun in Dubrovnik.

NO.text:
Norwegians spend Christmas Eve with family and New Year's Eve with friends: it is the second biggest celebration of the year. The table often holds a stuffed roast turkey with potatoes, sprouts, gravy and Waldorf salad, while some serve cured lamb ribs or roast pork belly instead. Dessert is rice cream or vanilla pudding, followed later by coffee, cakes and a glass of cognac. In the evening comes the King's New Year speech, a tradition dating back to Haakon VII.

As midnight approaches, everyone steps outside with rockets: private fireworks are allowed only from 18:00 to 02:00. In Oslo they are banned altogether inside the Ring 2 road, and to keep fireworks away from houses, Norwegian cities stage large public displays that people gather to watch in central squares. On 1 January it is the Prime Minister's turn to address the country.

traditions.title: Turkey and rice cream
traditions.text: Norwegians often build the New Year's Eve dinner around roast turkey with Waldorf salad and finish it with rice cream, coffee and a glass of cognac.

traditions.title: The King's speech
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December the King addresses the country on radio and TV, as kings have done since Haakon VII, and on 1 January the Prime Minister speaks.

traditions.title: Rockets until 2 a.m.
traditions.text: Private fireworks in Norway are allowed only from 18:00 to 02:00, and close to midnight everyone goes outside; in central Oslo, inside Ring 2, fireworks are banned.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Norway: Oslo | Time2Fest
meta.description: Norway welcomes 2027 at 23:00 UTC with roast turkey and rice cream, the King's New Year speech, rockets until 2 a.m. and public fireworks over the cities.

CG.text:
The last hours of the year in the Republic of the Congo are spent either in church or in bars and open-air maquis where the music plays until morning: in Brazzaville, from Bacongo to Talangaï, people dance to songs by Extra Musica. At home the table is laid, and between dishes everyone waits for midnight to exchange good wishes.

The first day of the year belongs to the family: saka-saka made from cassava leaves, beans, chicken, fresh and salted fish, and over the meal people look back on the year and make plans for the next. Towards evening whole families from Brazzaville head to the Corniche by the cable-stayed bridge to have their photo taken on the first day of the year.

traditions.title: Saka-saka at the family table
traditions.text: Families gather on 1 January for saka-saka made from cassava leaves, beans, chicken and fish, and sum up the year at the table.

traditions.title: Church or the maquis
traditions.text: Some greet midnight in church, others dance until morning in bars and open-air maquis.

traditions.title: A photo on the Corniche
traditions.text: On the evening of 1 January Brazzaville families stroll along the Corniche and have their photo taken by the cable-stayed bridge to remember the first day of the year.

meta.title: New Year in the Republic of the Congo | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Republic of the Congo greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: Brazzaville prays in church or dances in maquis, then shares saka-saka and walks the Corniche.

CH.text:
A pot of hot broth in the middle of the table means fondue chinoise: everyone dips their own pieces of meat into it, and at New Year it counts as the real national dish of Switzerland. In Appenzell the year is welcomed twice — on 31 December and again on 13 January, by the old Julian calendar. At dawn groups of Silvesterchläuse dressed as the “beautiful”, the “ugly” and the “beautifully ugly” go from farm to farm, form a circle, ring their bells and sing a wordless yodel.

Zurich hears its bells twenty minutes before midnight; they ring until 23:58. At 00:19 the lights go out in the city centre, and from 00:20 the Silvesterzauber fireworks light up the lake basin for a quarter of an hour. Entry is free, and the music on the lakeside goes on until morning. At midnight sharp, the New Year’s Marathon sets off in nearby Schlieren, on laps of 10.55 kilometres.

traditions.title: Fondue chinoise
traditions.text: Put a pot of hot broth on the table and let everyone cook their own pieces of meat in it — a Swiss Christmas and New Year classic.

traditions.title: Bells at dawn
traditions.text: In Appenzell on 31 December and 13 January the Silvesterchläuse visit farms: they form a circle, ring their bells and sing a wordless yodel to wish a happy year.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the lake
traditions.text: After midnight, Zurich gathers by the lake: at 00:19 the city-centre lights go out, then fireworks light up the lake basin for 15 minutes. Entry is free.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Switzerland: Zurich | Time2Fest
meta.description: Switzerland greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with fondue chinoise, bells and fireworks over Lake Zurich, and bell-ringing Silvesterchläuse at dawn in Appenzell.

SE.text:
A late shellfish dinner, sparkling wine and plenty of snacks: that is how Sweden sees out the year, with people gathered with family or friends, often over a three-course meal. In the last minute everyone counts down, and at midnight they shout «Gott nytt år!», pop the champagne, kiss and make New Year's resolutions. Big fireworks light up the cities, ships in the harbours sound their horns, and only people aged 18 and over may buy fireworks.

Stockholm has a ritual of its own: at the Skansen open-air museum, the poem «Nyårsklockan» is read exactly at midnight, a Swedish version of Tennyson's «Ring Out, Wild Bells» with the line «Ring, klocka, ring». It was first read there in 1895, television has shown the reading since 1977, and since 2014 a new reader has been chosen every year.

traditions.title: A shellfish dinner
traditions.text: Late on 31 December Swedes sit down to a festive dinner, often three courses with shellfish, and sparkling wine and snacks stay on the table until midnight.

traditions.title: «Ring, klocka, ring» at midnight
traditions.text: Since 1895 the poem «Nyårsklockan» has been read at midnight at Skansen in Stockholm; the reading is shown on television, and every year a new voice reads it.

traditions.title: «Gott nytt år!» and resolutions
traditions.text: Swedes count the last minute of the year out loud, shout «Gott nytt år!» at midnight, clink champagne glasses, share a New Year's kiss and make a resolution.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Sweden: Stockholm | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight Skansen hears «Ring, klocka, ring» and Sweden pops the champagne: how Swedes greet 2027 with a shellfish dinner, fireworks and ships' horns.

AD.text:
Twelve grapes, one for each stroke of the clock at midnight: in Andorra, whoever manages to eat them all is promised a happy year. Right after that, glasses of sparkling wine go up. The holiday falls at the height of the ski season: for the arrival of 2026 every slope at all three of the country's resorts was open, and on the evening of 31 December skiers came down the slope in Soldeu carrying lights.

On 5 January the Three Kings parade makes its way from Andorra la Vella, Europe's highest capital at 1,023 metres, to Escaldes-Engordany: in 2026 it had 18 floats and about 500 participants. The Christmas Village stays open until that day, and on 1 January 2026 the national orchestra played a New Year's concert of Strauss waltzes at the Congress Centre.

traditions.title: A grape per chime
traditions.text: At midnight eat one grape on each chime of the clock, then raise a glass of sparkling wine for a happy year.

traditions.title: A descent of lights
traditions.text: Last year on the evening of 31 December skiers in Soldeu came down a snowy slope with lights, then warmed up with hot chocolate.

traditions.title: New Year waltzes
traditions.text: On 1 January 2026 Andorra's national orchestra played the 'Paris–Vienna' concert of Strauss waltzes in the capital.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Andorra: Andorra la Vella | Time2Fest
meta.description: Andorra greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with twelve grapes on the midnight chimes, skiers with lights on the slopes of Soldeu and a Christmas village in the capital.

AL.text:
Roast turkey with përshesh, crumbled bread soaked in broth, is the star of the Albanian New Year dinner, which starts at around nine. The baklava is baked days in advance and glasses are filled with raki or local wine: a full table is a wish for plenty all year long. When religious holidays were banned, it was the night of 1 January that took over the decorated tree, still often called the New Year tree, and the gifts from the Grandfather of the New Year, so it remains the great family holiday of winter.

People from all over the country head to Skanderbeg Square in Tirana for an open-air concert. At midnight fireworks burst over the square, everyone hugs and calls out "Gëzuar Vitin e Ri!" The first and second of January are public holidays, so the celebration goes on for two more days.

traditions.title: Turkey with përshesh
traditions.text: The star of the New Year table is roast turkey with përshesh, bread soaked in turkey broth. Dessert is baklava, baked days ahead.

traditions.title: The New Year tree
traditions.text: In Albania the decorated tree is often called the New Year tree, and the presents under it come from Babagjyshi, the Grandfather of the New Year.

traditions.title: Midnight on Skanderbeg Square
traditions.text: An open-air concert on Tirana's main square greets midnight with fireworks: time to hug and wish "Gëzuar Vitin e Ri!"

meta.title: New Year in Albania: Tirana | Time2Fest
meta.description: Turkey with përshesh, baklava and fireworks over Skanderbeg Square in Tirana: Albania welcomes 2027 at midnight, 23:00 UTC, with an open-air concert.

AT.text:
At midnight a single bell sounds across Austria: the Pummerin of Vienna's St. Stephen's Cathedral, which rings only on special occasions. Radio and television carry its voice, followed by the waltz "The Blue Danube", and many people dance right in the living room or out in the street. Lucky charms are bought in advance: little pigs, chimney sweeps, horseshoes and fly agarics. Then on the morning of 1 January the Vienna Philharmonic's New Year's Concert rings out from the Great Hall of the Musikverein, and at the end the audience claps in time to the Radetzky March.

Meanwhile the Viennese head out onto the Silvesterpfad, the New Year's Eve trail: stages from Am Hof along the Graben to Stephansplatz play from two in the afternoon until two at night. Nobody sends up rockets here — they are banned in the city, and the official fireworks were dropped for the sake of people, animals and the environment. Instead there is a kiss at midnight and fish-shaped lucky biscuits, eaten starting from the fin.

traditions.title: The bell, then the waltz
traditions.text: When the Pummerin rings, raise your glass, and with the first bars of "The Blue Danube" ask someone to waltz — that is how the whole country greets the new year.

traditions.title: A charm from a New Year stall
traditions.text: From 27 to 31 December, the Viennese buy lucky charms at stalls all over the city — a little pig, a chimney sweep, a horseshoe or a fly agaric — and give them to each other for luck.

traditions.title: A concert on 1 January
traditions.text: At 11:15 the Vienna Philharmonic's New Year's Concert is shown on screens at Stephansplatz and by the giant wheel in the Prater; clap along in time to the Radetzky March.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Austria: Vienna | Time2Fest
meta.description: Austria rings in 2027 at 23:00 UTC with the Pummerin bell and a Blue Danube waltz, while Vienna parties on the Silvesterpfad with stages across the old town.

BE.text:
A rhyming letter on paper decorated with golden cherubs: that is how Flemish children greet their parents and godparents on the morning of 1 January, and they get a present or some money in return. The night before, Sint-Silvester, Belgians more often spend with friends than with family: they watch a comedian on TV sum up the year, and at midnight they kiss, wish each other luck and raise a glass of bubbly — including to those who are not there.

At the foot of the Atomium in Brussels, DJs play from nine in the evening; twenty minutes before midnight a laser show lights up the giant spheres, and at exactly twelve the city fireworks rise above them. Entry is free, and after midnight public transport runs free of charge until morning.

traditions.title: A letter for godparents
traditions.text: Write a rhyming New Year's letter on festive paper and read it aloud on the morning of 1 January to your parents or godparents — Flemish children do it and get a present in return.

traditions.title: A song at the door
traditions.text: On 31 December in the Kempen and the Hageland, children go door to door singing "Nieuwejaarke zoete" — keep some sweets or a few coins ready for them.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the Atomium
traditions.text: Brussels residents ride metro line 6 to the Atomium: at 23:40 a laser show starts on the spheres, the fireworks go up at midnight, and afterwards public transport takes everyone home for free.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Belgium: Brussels | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in 2027 (23:00 UTC) Belgium kisses and raises a glass, while Brussels lights lasers and fireworks at the Atomium. Next morning: rhyming letters.

DK.text:
Just before midnight, Danes climb onto chairs, and as the clock strikes twelve they all jump together, leaping into the new year. The evening starts at six, when the King gives his New Year's speech, a tradition dating back to Christian IX's toast in the 1880s. Then comes the festive dinner of boiled cod or stewed kale, rounded off with kransekage, a tower of almond rings, and a glass of champagne.

Copenhagen counts down the last seconds on City Hall Square to the strike of the city clock, and as soon as the bells ring the sky over the city bursts into light. The fireworks are set off by people themselves, which is allowed only on 31 December and 1 January. And on the first morning the bravest take a dip in the cold harbour.

traditions.title: Leap into the new year
traditions.text: Before midnight, stand on a chair with everyone around you and jump as the clock strikes: the Danish way to enter the new year.

traditions.title: Kransekage and champagne
traditions.text: At midnight, break off a ring of kransekage, the almond-marzipan cake, and wash it down with champagne, the Danish end to the New Year dinner.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the Lakes
traditions.text: To watch the whole city light up, Copenhageners gather on Queen Louise's Bridge over the Lakes: the sky is open in every direction.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Denmark: Copenhagen | Time2Fest
meta.description: Denmark meets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with a leap off a chair as the City Hall clock strikes, almond kransekage with champagne and fireworks over Copenhagen.

GQ.text:
Mass first, then dinner, and only then dancing — that is the order of New Year's Eve in Equatorial Guinea. The services of 31 December and 1 January are among the most important of the year: believers go to a mass of thanksgiving for the year gone by. From there families head to the festive table, and after dinner comes the secular side of the night — parties, discos or simply a stroll through streets hung with lights.

Malabo, the oldest city in the country, on the island of Bioko, gives the first day of the year to the Los Ángeles neighbourhood. Young people close off the streets, put speakers outdoors and dance in the open air almost until evening, in deliberately extravagant outfits, to songs by Equatoguinean musicians. People say it all began on Calle La Ronda; now Los Ángeles is the busiest place in town on 1 January.

traditions.title: Thanksgiving mass on 31 December
traditions.text: Many families see the year out in church: first they give thanks for the past twelve months, and only then sit down to the festive dinner.

traditions.title: Abalá and bushmeat
traditions.text: Holiday cooking means abalá — grated white malanga wrapped in banana leaf — bushmeat in palm oil and djacató, a vegetable like small aubergines. Some travel home to their village to see the wider family.

traditions.title: Dancing in Los Ángeles
traditions.text: On 1 January Malabo's young people gather in the Los Ángeles neighbourhood: speakers on the pavement, dancing in the closed-off streets, bright outfits and local music.

meta.title: New Year in Equatorial Guinea: Malabo | Time2Fest
meta.description: Equatorial Guinea greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: a thanksgiving mass, dinner with family, and on 1 January Malabo dances in the streets of Los Ángeles.

CZ.text:
A glass of sekt at midnight, a plate of chlebíčky — small open sandwiches — and, for some, boiled pork head with grated horseradish and apples: that is how Czechs see off Silvestr. The first of January is a double holiday here — New Year's Day and the Restoration Day of the Independent Czech State, born in 1993. Lunch is lentils, shaped like little coins, and pork, while poultry and fish are avoided so that luck won't fly or swim away. Then everyone goes for a walk: “As on New Year's Day, so all year round.”

Prague's night gathers on Old Town Square: from five in the evening live bands and DJs play there, and at midnight the crowd counts down the seconds together. There has been no city fireworks display for several years — back in 2019 the council chose quiet for residents and animals. Fireworks are banned in the historic centre, by the Vltava and in parks.

traditions.title: Lentils for luck
traditions.text: On 1 January cook lentils with pork — the coin-like grains promise money — and skip poultry and fish so your luck won't fly or swim away.

traditions.title: Chlebíčky and sekt
traditions.text: Make a few kinds of chlebíčky, small open sandwiches, for the evening and pop a bottle of Czech sparkling wine at midnight sharp.

traditions.title: Countdown on Old Town Square
traditions.text: On Old Town Square in Prague, music and DJs play from 5 pm, and at midnight the whole square counts down together. Fireworks are banned in the centre.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Czechia: Prague | Time2Fest
meta.description: Czechia greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with sekt and chlebíčky at midnight, a shared countdown on Prague's Old Town Square and lentils for money on 1 January.

GA.text:
Many people in Gabon spend the last evening of the year in church: at Sainte-Marie Cathedral, at Saint-Pierre and Sacré-Cœur, in the capital's Protestant churches they sing at the last service of the year and pray for health and prosperity. In the days before the holiday shops have queues as people buy food for the New Year's Eve dinner and the family meal on 1 January, a public holiday. On 2 January Libreville is still resting: roads are empty, few people turn up at work, and schools only reopen on the third.

At midnight thousands head to the seafront, where fireworks burst over the ocean for about half an hour. People film the sky on their phones, applaud the loudest rockets, and when the last one fades they shout 'Bonne année!' to each other.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the ocean
traditions.text: Libreville's seafront is the place to be at midnight: fireworks over the water last up to half an hour, and then everyone greets each other with 'Bonne année!'.

traditions.title: The last service of the year
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December the capital's churches sing and pray for a new year of health, happiness and prosperity.

traditions.title: Family meal on 1 January
traditions.text: Food is bought in advance: 1 January is a public holiday and a day for the family table, and on the 2nd the city is still taking it slow.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Gabon: Libreville | Time2Fest
meta.description: Gabon reaches 2027 at 23:00 UTC with fireworks over the ocean on Libreville's seafront, the year's last church service and 'Bonne année!' at midnight.

GI.text:
The Casemates clock strikes midnight, and confetti and fireworks fill the sky for about ten minutes. Gibraltar's party is put on by the government: bands and DJs play from half past ten in the evening until three in the morning, and the presenters count down the last seconds together with the whole square. People come as families and groups of friends, tourists celebrate alongside them, glasses of champagne go up, and from the stage come greetings to the residents of care homes and to everyone seeing in the year at home. The fireworks returned to Casemates for the start of 2026 after a break.

The festive days end on the evening of 5 January. The Three Kings' Cavalcade sets off from Casemates along Main Street to the Ince's Hall Theatre with its floats, and sweets are handed out to everyone lining the route.

traditions.title: Countdown under the Casemates clock
traditions.text: Casemates Square fills up before midnight: the presenters count down the last seconds, and as the clock strikes, confetti and fireworks go up over the square.

traditions.title: Champagne with the whole square
traditions.text: This is a family party: Gibraltarians see in the year with family and friends, raise a glass with the people around them and dance to the bands and DJs until three in the morning.

traditions.title: Sweets on Main Street
traditions.text: On the evening of 5 January, families line Main Street: the Three Kings' Cavalcade runs from Casemates to Ince's Hall, and sweets are handed out to everyone who comes.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Gibraltar | Time2Fest
meta.description: Gibraltar sees in 2027 on Casemates Square with a countdown under the clock, confetti, fireworks and dancing till 3am. Midnight there is 23:00 UTC.

HU.text:
Midnight in Hungary arrives with the national anthem: as soon as the countdown ends, the Himnusz plays, and many people stand up and sing along. Then glasses clink and a short "BUÉK!" rings out, the colloquial abbreviation of the wish for a happy new year. Szilveszter night is spent at home or at street parties, with frankfurters and horseradish and roast pork: the pig, they say, roots up luck from the ground. Chicken stays off the menu on New Year's Day because it scratches luck away, while lentils are cooked for money.

Budapest heads out to its squares and the banks of the Danube, the Christmas markets stay open late into the night, and night buses and tram 6 carry people home until morning. There is no big city fireworks show, and since 2025 private rockets have been allowed only from 20:00 to 2:00 and not in residential areas.

traditions.title: The anthem at midnight
traditions.text: When the countdown reaches zero, people stand up and sing the Himnusz, and only then clink glasses.

traditions.title: Roast pork, not chicken
traditions.text: Pork and frankfurters with horseradish go on the table, and on 1 January lentil soup is cooked for luck and money; chicken and fish wait for another day.

traditions.title: "BUÉK!" with a glass
traditions.text: Clinking glasses, Hungarians greet each other with a short "BUÉK!", their abbreviation of the wish for a happy new year.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Hungary: Budapest | Time2Fest
meta.description: Hungary greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC by singing the Himnusz, clinking glasses to a quick BUÉK and eating pork and lentils, while Budapest fills its Danube banks.

MC.text:
At midnight the traditional fireworks go up over Port Hercule, their lights reflected in the water between the yachts. Before that, the Mairie de Monaco throws a free party right in the Christmas Village on the quay: DJs play on two stages from nine in the evening until two in the morning. The other countdown spot is Place du Casino in Monte-Carlo, decked out in lights, where the official countdown of the year's last seconds rings out.

The holidays last longer than one night. In Monegasque families a round loaf, U Pan de Natale, topped with a cross of walnuts, sits on the table from Christmas until Epiphany among olive twigs and thirteen desserts. The Ferris wheel above the port turns into the first days of January, and on 26 January the harbour lights up again: a symbolic fishing boat is burned outside the Church of Saint Devota, followed by fireworks.

traditions.title: Fireworks over Port Hercule
traditions.text: At midnight the traditional fireworks rise over the harbour. People greet them on the port's quays, where the town council holds a free party with DJs until 2 am.

traditions.title: Countdown on Casino Square
traditions.text: The square in front of the Monte-Carlo Casino is decked out in lights, and this is where the official countdown of the year's last seconds rings out.

traditions.title: Bread with a walnut cross
traditions.text: The round U Pan de Natale, topped with a cross of walnuts, stays on the festive table among olive twigs and thirteen desserts right up to Epiphany.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Monaco | Time2Fest
meta.description: Monaco sees in 2027 with fireworks over Port Hercule, a free DJ party on the quay and the countdown on Place du Casino. Midnight in Monaco is 23:00 UTC.

MK.text:
North Macedonia welcomes the new year twice: on 31 December, before Christmas, which Orthodox believers celebrate on 7 January, and again on the evening of 13 January by the old church calendar. The first night is spent at home with family and friends or in restaurants, cafés and clubs, dancing to folk music as much as to modern hits, while children get their presents during the day. For the Old New Year a bread with a hidden coin goes on the table, bringing luck to whoever finds it, and that same evening the village of Vevčani turns out for a carnival said to be more than 1,400 years old.

Skopje sees the year out on Macedonia Square, where the tree is lit in mid-December: on the evening of the 31st a big concert plays there. At midnight fireworks crackle over the city, even though the city authorities and police have more than once asked people to hold back.

traditions.title: Bread with a coin
traditions.text: On the evening of 13 January, the Old New Year, families share a festive bread with a coin hidden inside; whoever gets the piece with it is lucky all year.

traditions.title: The Vevčani carnival
traditions.text: The village of Vevčani greets the Old New Year with a carnival: on 13 January costumed revellers poke fun at the year's events, and the custom is said to be over 1,400 years old.

traditions.title: Concert on Macedonia Square
traditions.text: On 31 December the people of Skopje see the year out in the open air: in the evening a concert by Macedonian pop singers starts on Macedonia Square.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in North Macedonia: Skopje | Time2Fest
meta.description: North Macedonia greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with a concert on Skopje's Macedonia Square, then again on 13 January with coin bread and the Vevčani carnival.

NG.text:
Detty December is what Nigerians call the festive season that runs from December into the first days of January, when the diaspora flies home and Lagos lives on concerts, parties and beaches. Many travel further still, to their home villages and family. And every celebration needs jollof, rice cooked in one pot with tomatoes, hot peppers and onions: in West Africa they say a party without jollof is just a meeting.

The night into 1 January itself is crossover night. However you enter the year, so it will be, which is why most Christians greet midnight in church, while others are in clubs and at parties to the crack of "knock-out" firecrackers. Since 2012 Lagos has staged a city-wide celebration: for 2025, Afrobeats stars played five venues at once, and the following year the governor cancelled the festivities and asked residents to pray.

traditions.title: Midnight at the service
traditions.text: Most Christians see in the year at church during a crossover service, praying and singing in the belief that the way you enter the year shapes all of it.

traditions.title: Smoky party jollof
traditions.text: No Detty December party goes without jollof: party rice is cooked over a wood fire outdoors, so it tastes of smoke and has a crusty layer at the bottom of the pot.

traditions.title: Afrobeats till dawn
traditions.text: Lagos greets the year in clubs, on beaches and at concerts; for 2025, Afrobeats stars played five city venues at the same time.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Nigeria: Lagos | Time2Fest
meta.description: Nigeria crosses into 2027 at 23:00 UTC with crossover services in church, smoky party jollof in Detty December and Afrobeats in Lagos clubs and on its beaches.

NL.text:
Two thousand songs chosen by the listeners themselves play on the radio from Christmas right up to midnight on 31 December: since 1999 the Top 2000 marathon has become a kind of countdown to the new year for the Dutch. Oud en Nieuw, "Old and New", is usually a cosy evening at home with family or friends. On the table are oliebollen, raisin doughnuts under a dusting of powdered sugar, and apple beignets.

The night into 2027 is the first without home fireworks: since 1 August 2026 rockets and firecrackers have been banned for private use, so the sky is left to professional shows, the biggest traditionally in Rotterdam. Amsterdam gave up private fireworks even earlier and greeted midnight with a light show on Museumplein. And on 1 January some sixty thousand people plunge into the icy sea at Scheveningen.

traditions.title: Oliebollen and beignets
traditions.text: At home people fry oliebollen, raisin doughnuts generously dusted with powdered sugar, and apple beignets; those who don't fry their own buy them from a street stall.

traditions.title: A shot from a milk churn
traditions.text: In the countryside people fire carbide instead of fireworks: the blast knocks a lid or a ball off a milk churn. Since 2014 carbidschieten has been national intangible heritage.

traditions.title: The New Year's dive
traditions.text: On 1 January some 60,000 people plunge into the cold sea at Scheveningen, and thousands more at dozens of beaches and lakes around the country.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in the Netherlands: Amsterdam | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Netherlands greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with sugar-dusted oliebollen, a first night without home fireworks, light shows in Amsterdam and a New Year's sea dive.

PL.text:
In Poland, 31 December is called Sylwester, after the name day of Sylvester: the Catholic Church remembers Pope Sylvester I that day, and folk speech also calls the evening the "fat eve". It is a night of loud parties and balls, toasts and fireworks; champagne is uncorked exactly at midnight, television carries big concerts across the country, and 1 January is a day off.

For years the busiest place of the night has been Kraków's Main Market Square: a free open-air concert draws up to two hundred thousand people, and midnight comes with fireworks over St. Mary's Basilica. Those who want to escape the city bustle head for the mountains, most often to Zakopane. In Warsaw, a big Christmas tree glows on Castle Square until January.

traditions.title: Champagne at midnight
traditions.text: On the stroke of twelve the champagne is uncorked: the first glass says goodbye to the old year and welcomes the new one.

traditions.title: A ball until morning
traditions.text: Sylwester is a night of balls and loud parties; those fleeing the city bustle dance in the new year in the mountains, most often in Zakopane.

traditions.title: Kraków's Main Square
traditions.text: In Kraków a free open-air concert plays on the Main Market Square, and at midnight fireworks burst over St. Mary's Basilica.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Poland: Warsaw | Time2Fest
meta.description: Poland greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with Sylwester balls and champagne at midnight, a free concert on Kraków's Main Square, Zakopane's mountains and Warsaw's tree.

SI.text:
In late December Slovenian children wait for a third gift-bringer: after Saint Nicholas (Miklavž) on 6 December and Božiček on Christmas Eve comes Dedek Mraz, Grandpa Frost. The painter Maksim Gaspari created his look in 1952, and his home was later “moved” to Mount Triglav. Slovenia takes two days off for the New Year, 1 and 2 January.

At midnight five minutes of fireworks light up Ljubljana from the castle hill, and concerts fill four squares from nine. The youngest gather on Congress Square in the afternoon and symbolically step into the new year at five. Lake Bled holds its Winter Fairytale: a concert on the promenade and a drone show at midnight.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the castle
traditions.text: Five minutes of fireworks from the castle hill open the year over Ljubljana, and concerts on four squares start as early as 21:00.

traditions.title: Dedek Mraz for the kids
traditions.text: Fairy-tale characters entertain children on Congress Square from 16:00, Dedek Mraz drops by, and at 17:00 the little ones symbolically greet the new year.

traditions.title: Winter Fairytale in Bled
traditions.text: On the Lake Bled promenade a concert plays on New Year's Eve, and at the stroke of midnight a drone show rises over the water.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Slovenia: Ljubljana | Time2Fest
meta.description: Slovenia meets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with five minutes of fireworks from Ljubljana's castle hill, concerts on four squares and a drone show over Lake Bled.

SJ.text:
In Svalbard, New Year arrives in the middle of the polar night: in Longyearbyen the sun does not appear from late October to mid-February. It is dark even at noon, but at this time of year the northern lights show up both by day, with reddish tones, and in the evening, greener. People have dinner with friends: the town's restaurants prepare tasting menus from local hunters' produce, and some start the evening in an old champagne cellar where miners and officials once collected their alcohol ration.

On New Year's Eve two joint fireworks displays rise over Adventfjorden, organised by the local council together with the town's businesses: at 19:00 so the children can see them, and at midnight. Pyrotechnicians launch them from the sea, and the lights can be seen from almost anywhere in Longyearbyen. The tradition will continue until at least 2030.

traditions.title: Two displays over the fjord
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve pyrotechnicians fire a joint display over Adventfjorden twice — at 19:00 for the children and at midnight; local businesses fund it together with the council.

traditions.title: Aurora instead of dawn
traditions.text: The sun does not rise in Longyearbyen from late October to mid-February, so the first day of the year is dark too, and in the polar night the northern lights can appear even by day.

traditions.title: The miners' cellar
traditions.text: The festive dinner here is made from local hunters' produce, and the evening sometimes starts in an old champagne cellar where miners once collected their alcohol ration.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Svalbard: Longyearbyen | Time2Fest
meta.description: Polar night, daytime aurora and two joint fireworks over Adventfjorden: Longyearbyen in Svalbard greets 2027 at local midnight, 23:00 UTC, in the dark.

SK.text:
In Slovakia, Silvester is the noisiest day of the year: firecrackers and rockets go off in Bratislava and other towns before noon and grow thicker towards midnight. People see the year out at parties, in pubs and on town squares, and after the countdown the national anthem plays on TV — in recent years some stations have played the Czechoslovak anthem at midnight in honour of the shared past. Glasses of champagne, «Šťastný nový rok!» — and instead of «thank you» the answer is «you too». The first of January is also the Day of the Establishment of the Slovak Republic in 1993, and lunch means lentils for money.

Bratislava has not staged its own fireworks for several years, for ecological and financial reasons. Instead, Hviezdoslav Square plays a recording of the Slovak Philharmonic's New Year's Eve concert, bands and DJs take the stage, everyone counts down together at midnight, and the Christmas markets stay open until one in the morning.

traditions.title: No poultry on the table
traditions.text: On 1 January Slovaks eat lentils for money and pork for plenty, and skip poultry so that luck does not fly away.

traditions.title: «You too!»
traditions.text: Clinking champagne glasses, people wish «Všetko dobré do nového roku!» — all the best in the new year — and answer not «thank you» but «you too».

traditions.title: Squares instead of fireworks
traditions.text: Bratislava greets midnight on Hviezdoslav and Franciscan Squares with bands, DJs until one and a shared countdown, while the markets pour a glass for the toast.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Slovakia: Bratislava | Time2Fest
meta.description: Slovakia welcomes 2027 at 23:00 UTC: the noisiest day of the year, the anthem after the countdown, lentils on 1 January and Bratislava squares with DJs.

SM.text:
A glass of bubbles and a slice of panettone — that is how 2026 arrived on Piazza Sant’Agata in the historic centre of San Marino: the free party «2000 Che Stories!», full of 2000s hits, ran from ten in the evening until two in the morning. There have been no fireworks for several years: since 2022 the midnight toast goes without a display, and animal-welfare campaigners want firecrackers banned for everyone else too. The table looks just like across the Italian border: lentils for money, cotechino or zampone.

The holidays on Mount Titano last longer than one night. «Il Natale delle Meraviglie» — markets, an ice rink and lights in the UNESCO-listed old town — runs from 20 December to 6 January, and on the first of January circus performers take to the streets. For the table there is bustrengo, a festive cake of honey, nuts and dried fruit.

traditions.title: A toast with panettone
traditions.text: At midnight on Piazza Sant’Agata people clink glasses of bubbles and share panettone, while a DJ plays 2000s hits until two.

traditions.title: Lentils for money
traditions.text: As in neighbouring Italy, the New Year table has lentils, round like coins, with cotechino or zampone beside them.

traditions.title: Holidays until 6 January
traditions.text: Until 6 January the old town keeps its markets and ice rink open, and on the first of January circus performers walk the streets.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in San Marino | Time2Fest
meta.description: San Marino greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC with a panettone toast on Piazza Sant’Agata, 2000s hits until two, lentils on the table and an ice rink below Titano.

TD.text:
Saint-Sylvestre — as New Year's Eve is called here, the French way — is loudest in the big cities, above all in N'Djamena. The evening starts with a festive family dinner, then come friends and dancing, while some spend it in prayer. Over half of Chadians are Muslim and about two in five are Christian, and 1 January is a day off for everyone.

The heart of the holiday is the Dary festival on Place de la Nation in N'Djamena: for two weeks all 23 provinces show their dances and crafts there, and on 31 December a New Year's Eve concert plays. To welcome 2026 the organisers announced a big fireworks display. And on New Year's Day vuvuzelas sound across the capital's neighbourhoods as people in new clothes fill the streets.

traditions.title: The Dary festival
traditions.text: Around New Year, Place de la Nation in N'Djamena becomes the country's showcase: all 23 provinces bring their dances and crafts, and on 31 December a concert plays.

traditions.title: Dinner with the family
traditions.text: New Year's Eve often begins with a festive dinner with relatives, followed by visits to friends and dancing. Some greet the night in prayer.

traditions.title: New clothes and vuvuzelas
traditions.text: On 1 January vuvuzelas sound through the capital's neighbourhoods, and crowds fill the streets, most of them in new festive clothes.

meta.title: New Year in Chad: N'Djamena | Time2Fest
meta.description: Midnight in N'Djamena falls at 23:00 UTC: Chad meets 2027 with family dinners and dancing, the Dary festival gathers 23 provinces and vuvuzelas sound.

TN.text:
Roast chicken on the table and a cake saved for midnight: that is how most Tunisians see in the new year — at home, with family and friends. Some book dinner at a restaurant or hotel, and gifts and flowers change hands. Cakes come from pastry shops or the home oven; in December they sell out fast, and in 2023 a festive cake cost 80–120 dinars. Kemia adds its own flavour to the evening: olives, broad beans with cumin, fennel with lemon. 1 January is a day off, while the Hijri New Year, Ras el Am, is marked separately with couscous and green mloukhia for a ‘green year’.

The capital welcomes visitors at this time of year: in bookings for the 2023 holidays, Tunis ranked fourth among French travellers’ favourite year-end destinations. Midnight here falls at 23:00 UTC.

traditions.title: Roast chicken at home
traditions.text: Most Tunisians see in the year at a family table with relatives and friends, and the main dish of the evening is roast chicken.

traditions.title: A cake for midnight
traditions.text: The festive cake is bought at a pastry shop or baked at home, and it is cut when the clock strikes midnight.

traditions.title: Flowers and gifts
traditions.text: Some spend the evening in restaurants and hotels, and loved ones exchange gifts and flowers that night.

meta.title: New Year in Tunisia: Tunis | Time2Fest
meta.description: Midnight in Tunis falls at 23:00 UTC: Tunisia greets 2027 at home over roast chicken, saves the cake for 00:00 and swaps gifts and flowers in restaurants.

VA.text:
Vatican City, the world's smallest state, ends the year with thanks. On 31 December the Pope leads First Vespers of the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God, in Saint Peter's Basilica, and the «Te Deum», an ancient hymn of thanksgiving for the passing year, fills the nave. Francis led it in 2024, and Leo XIV saw out 2025 the same way.

The first day of the year belongs to peace. On 1 January the basilica hosts Mass for the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God; since 1968 it has also been the World Day of Peace, created by Paul VI. Then the Pope prays the Angelus with the people in Saint Peter's Square, where a Christmas tree and a nativity scene have stood each season since 1982.

traditions.title: Te Deum on the last evening
traditions.text: On 31 December Saint Peter's Basilica sings the «Te Deum», a hymn of thanks for everything the passing year has brought.

traditions.title: A first day for peace
traditions.text: 1 January is the World Day of Peace: after Mass the Pope prays the Angelus together with the people in the square.

traditions.title: Tree and crib in the square
traditions.text: Every holiday season a tall Christmas tree and a life-size nativity scene go up in the middle of Saint Peter's Square, a custom since 1982.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Vatican City | Time2Fest
meta.description: Vatican City ends the year with a Te Deum in Saint Peter's Basilica and meets 2027 at 23:00 UTC; 1 January brings Mass, the World Day of Peace and the Angelus.

CI.text:
Muslims and Christians are almost equal in number in Côte d’Ivoire, so New Year’s Eve has two faces. For some it means church: praise, prayer and thanks for the year that is ending. For others it means the maquis, open-air cafés with music, while grilled chicken and fish sell fast on the streets that night. 1 January is a day off for everyone.

Abidjan gets ready early: every December since 2011 the city dresses up in the “Abidjan, Ville Lumière” illuminations. At midnight into 2025, fireworks rose from the Charles de Gaulle and Félix Houphouët-Boigny bridges over the Ébrié Lagoon. Yopougon parties in the streets with bands and DJs, while Plateau and Cocody keep to quieter gala dinners.

traditions.title: Thanks for the year
traditions.text: Abidjan’s parishes are full on New Year’s Eve: believers meet midnight with praise and prayer, giving thanks for the year that is ending.

traditions.title: Fireworks from the bridges
traditions.text: At midnight fireworks go up from the bridges over the lagoon and at the Koumassi crossroads; thousands watch from the shores and bridges.

traditions.title: Chicken and fish off the grill
traditions.text: On New Year’s Eve chicken and fish braised over charcoal sell fast on the streets of Abobo. Grill chicken or fish at home and start the year the Abidjan way.

meta.title: New Year in Côte d’Ivoire: Abidjan | Time2Fest
meta.description: Côte d’Ivoire meets 2027 at 00:00 UTC: in Abidjan, fireworks from the bridges over the Ébrié Lagoon, thanksgiving in churches and street parties in Yopougon.

FO.text:
Bonfires on the hills and a sky full of rockets: that is how the Faroe Islands see out the old year. Bonfires are one of the best-loved New Year traditions, though the fire brigade sometimes bans them because of the wind, and the weather can be wild enough that on the island of Nólsoy the 2020 celebration was moved to 3 January. The best-known night is in Vágur in the south of the archipelago: at 23:45 a torch parade sets off, at midnight everyone sings a hymn together, a boat is set alight and the biggest fireworks show in the islands begins. There used to be ‘New Year villages’ too, where neighbours gathered to visit and dance.

Tórshavn meets midnight at 00:00 UTC with private fireworks over the harbour: even in 17 m/s winds in 2020, rockets and red parachute flares filled the town’s sky.

traditions.title: Bonfires on the last night
traditions.text: A bonfire on New Year's Eve is one of the best-loved Faroese traditions; when a strong wind blows, the fire brigade bans them.

traditions.title: Rockets over the harbour
traditions.text: At midnight private fireworks fill the sky over Tórshavn, red parachute flares among them.

traditions.title: Torches and a burning boat
traditions.text: Vágur's torch parade meets at midnight, people sing a hymn, a boat is set alight and the biggest fireworks show in the Faroes begins.

meta.title: New Year in the Faroe Islands: Tórshavn | Time2Fest
meta.description: Tórshavn reaches midnight at 00:00 UTC: the Faroe Islands greet 2027 with hilltop bonfires, rockets over the harbour and a torch parade in Vágur.

GH.text:
White clothes, hymns and testimonies until dawn: that is how most Ghanaians see the year out. Seven in ten people in the country are Christians, so on 31 December churches are full from the evening on: the night service, known here as watch night or crossover, carries on with prayer, praise and thanksgiving into the early hours of 1 January.
